knobs.code_doc: If ``True`` (default), blind the columns written to ``posterior_samples.npz`` / ``samples.h5`` so no stored artifact holds an absolute value. If ``False``, only human-facing summaries/plots are blinded and the raw samples remain absolute.
knobs.curated_html: If true, the blinded columns are also blinded in the stored artifacts (posterior_samples.npz / samples.h5) so no file on disk holds an absolute value. If false, only human-facing summaries and plots are blinded and raw samples stay absolute.

knobs.code_doc: Master switch. When ``False`` the pipeline behaves exactly as before.
knobs.curated_html: Master switch. Blinding subtracts the posterior location (mean/median) of each blinded parameter, so the analyst sees only shape and width — never the absolute value — until the collaboration unblinds. The subtracted offsets are sealed (see encrypt); an offset-free blinding_manifest.json records the frozen conventions. When false the pipeline behaves exactly as before.
warnings: mode and reference are chosen once and frozen per project — the pipeline refuses to mix conventions across runs sharing an output dir (TDCOSMO policy).

knobs.code_doc: If ``True`` (default), the offsets are ENCRYPTED under a secret key and sealed to ``blinding_key.json`` (ciphertext only — safe to leave in the run directory; unblinding is impossible without the key). If ``False``, the legacy plaintext ``blinding_offsets.json`` is written instead.
knobs.curated_html: If true, the offsets are encrypted under a secret key and sealed to blinding_key.json (ciphertext only — safe to leave in the run directory; unblinding is impossible without the key). If false, the legacy plaintext blinding_offsets.json is written instead.

knobs.code_doc: Secret key/passphrase for encryption. If ``None`` (default), the key is read from the ``key_env_var`` environment variable, and if that is unset a fresh random key is generated. Providing the key here is discouraged (it lands in the config file); prefer the env var.
knobs.curated_html: The secret that encrypts the blinding offsets. Order of lookup: this key, then the environment variable named by key_env_var (ALPACA_BLINDING_KEY), then a blinding_secret.key already in 05_posterior/samples/; otherwise a new key is generated at the start of the run and written there (unless write_key_file is false). The same key seals the posterior and the blinded entries of the GD sidecars (best_fit_params_full.npz).
warnings: Do not put the key in the config: the config is copied into every run folder. Use the environment variable, set inside the job script.

knobs.code_doc: Environment variable to read the secret key from when ``key`` is None. Default ``"ALPACA_BLINDING_KEY"``. Set to ``None`` to disable.
knobs.curated_html: Environment variable to read the secret key from when key is null. Set to null to disable env lookup entirely.

knobs.curated_html: "absolute" shows x − mean(x) (physical units, zero-centred); "fractional" shows (x − mean(x)) / mean(x) (dimensionless relative deviations).

knobs.curated_html: Explicit blind-set, overriding scenario when not null.

knobs.curated_html: Location statistic subtracted from the blinded parameters. Policy default is "mean".

knobs.code_doc: Preset blind-set (see ``alpaca.utils.blinding.SCENARIO_PARAMS``). Ignored when ``parameters`` is given. For systems already modelled in the literature (e.g. WFI2033-4723) use ``"previously_analyzed"``.

warnings: blinding_secret.key IS the secret: move it out of the run folder (to whoever decides on unblinding), or anyone with access to the folder can unblind.

knobs.code_doc: Optional layout stamp (1 = legacy, 2 = current). Not needed: the layout is detected from the keys, and ALPACA no longer writes the stamp.
knobs.curated_html: Optional layout stamp: 2 = the current layout (run, data, mass, light, stages, psf, likelihood, sampling, plotting, blinding), 1 = the legacy flat layout. You do not need it: ALPACA detects the layout from the keys, and the copy written to <run>/config/config.json no longer carries it.

knobs.code_doc: If set (< the loaded image size), the pipeline CENTER-CROPS the loaded image/noise to this size for ALL normal modelling (stages 1/2/3, sampling). The full loaded image is retained ONLY for the lens-light refit (LensLightRefitConfig), which fits the parametric lens light on the larger frame for better outer-profile / sky constraints; its cutout-invariant parameters transfer back to the cropped model unchanged. None = use the loaded image at its native size everywhere.
knobs.curated_html:
If set (and smaller than the loaded image), the pipeline center-crops the loaded image and noise map to this many pixels per side for every normal modelling stage and sampling. A full-frame data.likelihood_mask_path is center-cropped with the same offset; an already cutout-sized likelihood mask is accepted unchanged.

The full loaded frame is retained for the lens-light refit, which fits the parametric light on the larger frame for better outer-profile and sky constraints. Its cutout-invariant parameters transfer back to the cropped model unchanged, and its separate mask must match the full frame.

knobs.code_doc: Radius (arcsec) within which the lens-galaxy centre is refined from the seed position. Shrink for asymmetric lenses where a bright point-source image lies within the default 0.5" of the seed (otherwise the refinement locks onto the PS image instead of the lens galaxy).
knobs.curated_html: Radius within which the lens-galaxy centre is refined from the seed position. Shrink it for asymmetric systems where a bright point-source image lies within the search radius — otherwise the refinement locks onto the quasar image instead of the galaxy.

knobs.code_doc: Optional path to a boolean mask file (``.npy`` or ``.fits``). When provided, only ``True`` pixels contribute to the likelihood.
knobs.curated_html:
Optional boolean mask for the main lens-model likelihood — companions, diffraction spikes, cosmic-ray residuals, and detector defects. Only True pixels contribute; null disables the mask.

The .npy or .fits array may match either the modelling cutout or the original full science frame. When data.cutout_size is active and a full-frame mask is supplied, ALPACA center-crops it with exactly the same offset as the image and noise map. A cutout-sized mask is used directly.

This mask belongs to the main fit and is distinct from the full-frame light.lens.refit.mask_path. The same full-frame file may be used for both paths only when its pixel selection is intentionally suitable for both fits.
warnings: A line-of-sight perturber's LIGHT is modelled only when its catalog entry has a lens_light block — mask every other perturber galaxy here or its flux is fitted by the lens light / source and biases the fit.

knobs.code_doc: Number of point-source images to auto-detect. ``None`` (default) detects 4, exactly as before the key was honoured; images that are not detected are recovered near the supplied approximate ``image_positions``. Set it explicitly (e.g. 2 for doubles, 6 for six-image systems) to detect that many peaks directly.
knobs.curated_html: Number of point images to detect automatically. null (default) detects 4; images that are not found are then recovered near the approximate positions you supply (IMAGE_POSITIONS). Set it for other image counts, e.g. 2 for a double, or more than 4 for a system with extra images.

knobs.code_doc: Detector pixel scale in arcsec/pixel.
knobs.curated_html: Detector pixel scale of the science image. Read it from your FITS header (CD1_1/CD2_2 or D001SCAL). Common values: drizzled HST/WFC3 = 0.04, JWST/NIRCam short-wave = 0.031. Everything angular in the pipeline (masks, priors on offsets, PS separation) is expressed in arcsec and converted with this scale, so an incorrect value silently corrupts the whole geometry.

knobs.code_doc: Radius (arcsec) of the central mask around the lens centre that is excluded from point-source detection. Shrink this when one of the images sits close to the lens galaxy.
knobs.curated_html: Radius of the central mask around the lens-galaxy centre that is excluded from point-source detection, so the bright lens core is not picked up as a fifth image. Shrink it when a genuine quasar image sits close to the lens galaxy (small-separation quads, fold configurations).

knobs.code_doc: Minimum fraction of the brightest unmasked peak for a local maximum to be accepted as a point-source candidate. Lower this for high-magnification-ratio quads where the faintest image is much dimmer than the brightest.
knobs.curated_html: Minimum fraction of the brightest unmasked peak for a local maximum to count as a point-source candidate. Lower it (e.g. to 0.05) for high-magnification-ratio quads where the faintest image is far dimmer than the brightest; raising it suppresses spurious detections from bright arc knots.

knobs.code_doc: Minimum separation (arcsec) between detected point-source images. ``None`` (default) resolves to ``2 x pix_scale`` so it tracks the detector sampling automatically.
knobs.curated_html: Minimum separation between detected point-source images. Local maxima closer than this get merged into one candidate. Two native pixels is a safe default; raise it if noise spikes near an image split one quasar image into two detections.

knobs.code_doc: Source-plane supersampling factor for the forward model. The source grid is ``source_oversample`` times finer than the data pixels and downsampled on output. Memory scales ~quadratically. Note: the supersampling factor of the INPUT PSF lives in ``psf.input.oversample`` (it describes the provided PSF file, not the observation).
knobs.curated_html: Source-plane supersampling factor of the forward model: the internal source grid is this many times finer than the data pixels and is downsampled on output. Memory scales roughly quadratically. 3 is usually plenty; 5 adds marginal accuracy at ~2.8× the memory.

knobs.code_doc: Share one centre between the Sérsic components.
Share one ellipticity between the Sérsic components.
knobs.curated_html: Couple the ellipticities of all Sersic lens-light components: L2/L3 share e1/e2 with L1. Removes four latents from a triple-Sersic model and prevents the components from twisting against each other — recommended when the extra Sersics are meant as radial-profile freedom, not isophote-twist freedom.

knobs.code_doc: Upper bound on the lens-light ellipticity components |e1|, |e2| (default 0.4).
Lens-light model of the GD stage 1 (e.g. 'sersic', 'double-sersic', 'triple-sersic', 'MGE+double-sersic').
knobs.curated_html:
Lens-light model of the multistart (stage 1) and, unless the refit changes it, of stage 3:

  • "sersic": one Sérsic profile;
  • "double-sersic": bulge + envelope;
  • "triple-sersic": a third component for the core;
  • "MGE": a multi-Gaussian expansion replaces the Sérsics;
  • "MGE+double-sersic" / "MGE+triple-sersic": the Sérsics carry the profile, a small Gaussian stack absorbs core structure.

null derives the model from the legacy booleans (use_double_sersic_lens, use_triple_sersic_lens, use_mge_lens_light, mge_as_correction), still accepted in old configs. The number of MGE components is set in light.lens.mge.

knobs.code_doc: Number of Gaussians in the MGE lens-light model.
knobs.curated_html: Number of Gaussian components in the MGE stack, log-spaced in width between mge_sigma_min and mge_sigma_max. More components give smoother radial-profile freedom at the cost of one amplitude latent each.

knobs.code_doc: Largest MGE width (arcsec).
knobs.curated_html: Width of the widest MGE Gaussian. In correction mode keep this small (a few tenths of an arcsec) so the stack stays a core correction; in full-MGE mode it must reach the lens-light envelope scale.

knobs.code_doc: Smallest MGE width (arcsec).
knobs.curated_html: Width of the narrowest MGE Gaussian. Values well below the PSF width buy nothing — the convolution washes them out.

knobs.code_doc: Optimization budget of the light-only fit.
knobs.curated_html: Optimization budget of the light-only fit.

knobs.code_doc: Build a REFIT-ONLY arc annulus (arcsec, centred on the point-source centroid = the Einstein-ring centre) instead of reusing the CF arc mask. Strongly recommended whenever ``mask_arc`` or ``ps_sigma_clip_within="arc"`` is used: the CF mask is sized for SOURCE reconstruction and is far too wide for a light fit — a typical is a 0.7-2.8" annulus, and removing it costs 1.264 -> 1.879 in GD chi2 because it deletes the whole band where the Sersic R_e lives, leaving the profile there as bare interpolation. A narrow annulus bracketing the ring removes the arc flux without that damage. ``None`` for both (default): with ``mask_arc`` or ``ps_sigma_clip_within="arc"`` the annulus is built AUTOMATICALLY  from the image radii about the main-deflector centre of the current solution: [min r_i - w, max r_i + w], w = 0.2 x mean r_i (``lens_light_refit.AUTO_ARC_HALFWIDTH_FRAC``); the CF arc mask is then not used by the refit. Only without point-source positions does the refit fall back to the CF arc mask.
knobs.curated_html:
Inner radius (arcsec, about the main-deflector centre) of an arc annulus used ONLY by the lens-light refit, with mask_arc or ps_sigma_clip_within: "arc". null for both radii (default) builds the annulus automatically from the image radii of the current solution: [min ri − w, max ri + w] with w = 0.2 × mean ri. Without point-image positions the refit falls back to the correlated-field arc mask.

Do not reuse the correlated-field arc mask for the light fit: it is sized for the source and much too wide, and removing that whole band deletes the region where the Sérsic effective radius is constrained. A narrow annulus around the ring removes the arc flux without that damage.

knobs.code_doc: Build a REFIT-ONLY arc annulus (arcsec, centred on the point-source centroid = the Einstein-ring centre) instead of reusing the CF arc mask. Strongly recommended whenever ``mask_arc`` or ``ps_sigma_clip_within="arc"`` is used: the CF mask is sized for SOURCE reconstruction and is far too wide for a light fit — a typical is a 0.7-2.8" annulus, and removing it costs 1.264 -> 1.879 in GD chi2 because it deletes the whole band where the Sersic R_e lives, leaving the profile there as bare interpolation. A narrow annulus bracketing the ring removes the arc flux without that damage. ``None`` for both (default): with ``mask_arc`` or ``ps_sigma_clip_within="arc"`` the annulus is built AUTOMATICALLY  from the image radii about the main-deflector centre of the current solution: [min r_i - w, max r_i + w], w = 0.2 x mean r_i (``lens_light_refit.AUTO_ARC_HALFWIDTH_FRAC``); the CF arc mask is then not used by the refit. Only without point-source positions does the refit fall back to the CF arc mask.
knobs.curated_html: Outer radius (arcsec) of the refit-only arc annulus; must exceed arc_mask_inner_radius. null = automatic (see there).

knobs.code_doc: Width (arcsec) of the Gaussian prior on the per-component centre offsets of the refit light (lopsidedness). Only used when `uncouple_centers` is true. Default 0.05″.
Seed the Sersic indices distinctly (2.5/1/4) instead of all at 3.0. None = follow smooth_bounds.
knobs.curated_html: Start the Sérsic indices of the refit components at different values (2.5 / 1 / 4) instead of all at 3. null (default) follows smooth_bounds.

knobs.code_doc: : Prior half-width for the refit ellipticities (e1/e2 bounded : independently). None -> inherit model.lens_light_ellipticity_max.
Gaussian prior width on the per-component ellipticity DELTAS (twist amplitude); only used when uncouple_ellipticities is True.
knobs.curated_html: Gaussian prior width on the per-component ellipticity DELTAS (the twist amplitude); only used when uncouple_ellipticities is on.

Master switch for the staged lens-light refit. When enabled, after the cf_warmstart stage the pipeline subtracts the current (source + point-source) model from the data and fits the lens light ALONE on the residual — no mass model involved — then carries that light into cf_joint (fixed or free per stages.cf_joint.lens_light). The sampling stage frees the light again, warm-started from the refit values.

knobs.code_doc: If True (default), perturbers IN FRONT of the lens plane are frozen at their stage-2 values during stage 3 while the refit light is frozen. Foreground masses deflect the grid the main-plane light is evaluated on; letting them move drags the frozen galaxy render sub-pixel across the cusp and prints a core dipole. With a frozen light, nothing else that sets its frame may move.

With the light free in cf_joint (``stages.cf_joint.lens_light = "free"``), start cf_joint's lens-light and sky sites from the refit (default True): that is the point of the refit, a light fitted on the full loaded frame. The refit's components are assigned to the model's slots by the permutation that needs the least clipping of R_e and n into the slot priors, then clipped just inside the prior support. False = the legacy start from the stage-1 light, with every component the refit added at its prior centre (the refit result is then computed and not used).
knobs.curated_html: With the lens light free in stage 3 (stages.cf_joint.lens_light: "free"), start stage 3's lens-light and sky parameters from the refit (default true): that is the purpose of the refit, a light profile fitted on the full frame. The refit's components are matched to the stage-3 model's components by the assignment that needs the least clipping of Re and n into their priors. false = the legacy start from the stage-1 light (the refit result is then computed but not used).

knobs.code_doc: Zero-weight the CF ARC MASK region during the light-only fit. The refit target ``data - (source+PS)`` still carries the arc when ``simple_source="stage1"`` (the smooth stage-1 source cannot reproduce arc detail), and that leftover flux is real signal the parametric light must not chase. Excluding it POSITIONALLY removes it without the one-sided selection bias a residual clip introduces — membership is decided by geometry, not by how far the data sits above the current model. Default True . Needs an arc mask (an active ``model.corr_field.arc_mask`` or the refit-only annulus below); without one the refit warns and fits unmasked.
knobs.curated_html:
Give the arc region zero weight in the light-only refit (default true). The refit target, data − (source + point images), still contains arc flux that the smooth stage-1 source could not reproduce; the lens-light profile must not chase it. The arc is removed by position (an annulus), not by a residual clip, so the selection does not depend on the current model.

The annulus is arc_mask_inner_radius / arc_mask_outer_radius, automatic when both are null. Without an annulus or an arc mask the refit warns and fits unmasked.

knobs.code_doc: Bigger-cutout refit: when DataConfig.cutout_size crops the modelling image, the refit runs on the FULL loaded frame instead. mask_path is the likelihood mask for THAT larger frame (masks field galaxies outside the lens; keeps lens+sky active). Its shape must match the full loaded image, not the cropped model. Required when the full frame is larger than the modelling cutout.
knobs.curated_html:
Mask for the lens-light refit only. When data.cutout_size crops the modelling image, the refit deliberately runs on the full loaded frame so the galaxy's faint wings and sky remain constrained. This mask must therefore match the full frame—not the modelling cutout—and should exclude field galaxies while keeping the lens and sky active.

Unlike a full-frame data.likelihood_mask_path, this mask is not center-cropped. The same full-frame file can be assigned to both settings only when the desired pixel selection is genuinely identical.

knobs.code_doc: MGE components for the refit (None = model.mge_n_components).
knobs.curated_html: MGE components for the refit light model; null inherits light.lens.mge.n_components.

knobs.code_doc: Upper bound of the Sérsic index n of every refit component (default 8). Pairs with `n_sersic_min`; a component at either bound is a warning sign (guide §9.3).
knobs.curated_html: Upper bound of the Sérsic index n of every refit component (default 8); pairs with n_sersic_min. A component at either bound is a warning sign.

knobs.code_doc: Sersic-index bounds for the refit. Default floor 0.2 (measured: the data can want a near-Gaussian core; a 0.5 floor blocks it and prints an over-bright annulus around the core). n = 0.5 is a GAUSSIAN, and a triple-sersic refit can drive a component onto it from above even with smooth bounds — i.e. the fit wants a Gaussian core component and the floor is what stops it. Lowering it is the one evidence-backed knob, but there is little room: herculens approximates b_n = 1.9992*n - 0.3271, which reaches ZERO at n = 0.164, below which the profile degenerates to flat. Below ~0.35 treat the profile as a fitting basis, not a Sersic.
knobs.curated_html: Sersic-index floor for the refit (n_sersic_max = 8.0 is the ceiling). The worked example uses 0.2, allowing a triple-Sersic refit to use a very shallow core component. There is little room below it: the Sersic normalisation approximation reaches zero at n ≈ 0.164, below which the profile degenerates to flat. Below ~0.35, treat the profile as a flexible fitting basis rather than a conventional Sersic component.

knobs.code_doc: Complexity of the refit light model. "same" = the main model's ``lens_light``; otherwise any lens_light option ("sersic", "double-sersic", "triple-sersic", "MGE", "MGE+double-sersic", "MGE+triple-sersic") — it may be MORE complex than the first try. From the refit onward this becomes the lens-light parametrization.
knobs.curated_html: Complexity of the refit light model. "same" reuses light.lens.initial; any other lens-light option ("sersic", "double-sersic", "triple-sersic", "MGE", "MGE+double-sersic", "MGE+triple-sersic") may be MORE complex than the first try. From the refit onward this becomes the lens-light parametrization of the whole pipeline. The shipped example uses "triple-sersic". (This key was previously spelled lens_light; the old spelling is still accepted on input.)

knobs.code_doc: Radius (arcsec) of the region around each point source that is downweighted or masked. Used by ``"downweight"``/``"mask"`` only; under ``"sigma_clip"`` the region is still computed, but purely as a diagnostic overlay (it carries zero weight in the fit).
knobs.curated_html: Radius of the region around each point source that is downweighted or masked. Used by "downweight"/"mask"; under "sigma_clip" the region is still computed but only as a diagnostic overlay (zero weight in the fit).

knobs.code_doc: DEPRECATED alias kept for old configs: ``True`` means ``ps_treatment="mask"``. Ignored when ``ps_treatment`` is set explicitly.

Clip threshold in sigma for ``ps_treatment="sigma_clip"``; ``None`` resolves to the 4.0 default. Ignored in the other modes. Setting it without a ``ps_treatment`` selects ``"sigma_clip"`` (the pre- "clip alone" idiom, ``ps_mask=false`` + ``ps_downweight_radius=0``).
knobs.curated_html: Clip threshold in sigma for ps_treatment="sigma_clip"; null resolves to 4.0 whenever clipping is active. Ignored in the other modes.

knobs.code_doc: Binary-dilate the clipped set by this many pixels (default 1). A bare threshold clips the PSF CORE but leaves the wings just below it, and those wings are exactly the flux the Sersic would otherwise absorb; one ring of growth removes them. 0 disables the growth.
Max sigma-clip reweight passes (default 3); stops early once the clipped-pixel set stops changing.
knobs.curated_html: Maximum sigma-clip reweight passes; stops early once the clipped-pixel set stops changing. Related fine-tuning: ps_sigma_clip_grow (int, default 1) binary-dilates the clipped set — a bare threshold clips the PSF core but leaves the wings just below it, and one ring of growth removes exactly the flux the Sersic would otherwise absorb; ps_sigma_clip_within ("all" | "arc" | "ps_aperture", default "all") confines where the clip may reject — an unrestricted clip also deletes lens-light pixels wherever the parametric profile fits badly (typically the galaxy core), which is the opposite of its purpose.

knobs.code_doc: Where the residual clip may reject: ``"all"`` (default), ``"arc"`` (only inside the arc mask) or ``"ps_aperture"``. An unrestricted clip also deletes lens-light pixels wherever the parametric profile fits badly — typically the galaxy CORE — which is the opposite of its purpose; confining it keeps the light intact.

How the light-only fit protects itself from point-source residuals. The three modes are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE — this is the single knob: - ``"downweight"`` (default): inflate sigma 100x inside ``ps_downweight_radius`` of each point source. - ``"mask"``: zero-weight that same region entirely. - ``"sigma_clip"``: no positional PS region at all. Fit once over the whole frame, then reject pixels by RESIDUAL — anything with ``|target - light| / sigma > ps_sigma_clip`` is zero-weighted and the light is refit, iterating until the clipped set is stable. Rejects PS cores, cosmic rays and neighbour-galaxy wings wherever they actually land instead of trusting a fixed radius, and keeps every good pixel a positional mask would have thrown away (the PS aperture covers a large part of the galaxy's own core). Whichever mode is used, it is internal to the refit only — the likelihood mask used by the main pipeline is untouched.
knobs.curated_html:
How the light-only fit protects itself from point-source residuals — the three modes are mutually exclusive and this is the single knob:

  • "downweight" — inflate sigma 100× inside ps_downweight_radius of each point source.
  • "mask" — zero-weight that same region entirely.
  • "sigma_clip" — no positional region at all: fit over the whole frame, then reject pixels by RESIDUAL (|target − light|/sigma > ps_sigma_clip) and refit, iterating until the clipped set is stable. Rejects PS cores, cosmic rays and neighbour-galaxy wings wherever they actually land, and keeps every good pixel a positional mask would have thrown away.

Whichever mode is used, it is internal to the refit only — the main pipeline's likelihood mask is untouched.

knobs.code_doc: Source used for the (source+PS) subtraction the lens light is refit on. "cf" (default): the stage-2 correlated-field source — but a noisy CF source leaks flux to the cutout edges and contaminates the refit target. "stage1": use the SMOOTH stage-1 shapelets source instead, so the refit target is clean; the CF source then fits the residual arc detail in stage 3 with the light frozen. Decouples the light refit from CF noise.
knobs.curated_html: Which source model is subtracted (with the point sources) to build the refit target. "cf": the cf_warmstart correlated-field source — but a noisy CF source leaks flux to the cutout edges and contaminates the target. "stage1": the SMOOTH stage-1 shapelets source, so the target is clean; the CF source then fits the residual arc detail in cf_joint with the light frozen. Decouples the light refit from CF noise.

knobs.code_doc: If set (MJy/sr), the UNIFORM sky is FIXED to this value during the refit (e.g. an externally calculated sky level). To hold the sky at the REFIT's value in cf_joint and sampling, set ``light.sky_background_fixed_amp = "refit"``.
knobs.curated_html: If set (surface-brightness units of the image), the UNIFORM sky component is FIXED to this value during the refit — e.g. an externally calibrated sky level.

knobs.code_doc: Bound the Sersic index and ellipticities with BIJECTIONS (n = 0.5 + 7.5*sigmoid, e = 0.4*tanh) instead of ``jnp.clip``. Default False. A hard clip has ZERO gradient outside its bounds, so a parameter Adam pushes past one is dead and can never return — not a constraint but a trap, and the direct cause of triple-Sersic refits landing on ``n_sersic = 0.500`` exactly with unphysical companions. Also seeds the Sersic indices distinctly (2.5/1/4, matched to the R_e seeds) rather than all at 3.0, which is a symmetric start the components readily collapse out of.
knobs.curated_html: Bound the Sérsic index and the ellipticities of the refit components with smooth bijections (n = 0.5 + 7.5·sigmoid, e = 0.4·tanh) instead of a hard clip. Default false. A hard clip has zero gradient beyond its bound, so a parameter pushed past it cannot come back: with false, check that no component sits exactly at a bound of n or e. true also starts the Sérsic indices at different values (see distinct_n_init).

knobs.code_doc: Per-component CENTER deltas (lopsidedness); analogous to the twist.
knobs.curated_html: Per-component centre deltas (lopsidedness) — the positional analogue of the ellipticity twist. center_shift_sigma (float, default 0.05) is the Gaussian prior width on the deltas. Two further stability switches share this block: freeze_foreground_perts (bool, default true) freezes foreground-plane perturbers at their warmstart values while the refit light is frozen in cf_joint — foreground masses deflect the grid the light is evaluated on, and letting them move drags the frozen galaxy render sub-pixel across the cusp, printing a core dipole.

Give each refit component (each Sersic and the MGE stack) its OWN ellipticity instead of one shared shape — allowing isophote twist and radial flattening gradients. A shared-ellipticity model of a real galaxy prints a characteristic quadrupolar residual; uncoupling removes it.

knobs.code_doc: Lensed point sources (quasar images). false = galaxy-galaxy mode.
knobs.curated_html: Whether the lens has point images (lensed quasar or supernova). false = galaxy–galaxy mode: no point-image detection, no image positions or fluxes, no time delays, astrometry or ray-shooting terms, no point-image overlays. The joint PSF and the staged workflow (refit, correlated-field source) still run; the PSF is then constrained by the STARRED seed, its priors and the extended light.
warnings: With point sources off, validation switches off (one grouped message in the log): likelihood.use_time_delays, use_rayshoot_consistency, use_image_pos_offsets, noise_model.noise_boost and noise_model.use_psf_error_map; psf.mode "iterative" becomes "fixed" (it needs point images). likelihood.astrometry_mode can stay "image_plane": without two point images no astrometry term is built.

knobs.code_doc: Render point sources by FFT convolution instead of direct PSF placement.
knobs.curated_html: Experimental (anomaly-005 fix): render point sources by exact Fourier-shift placement instead of the bilinear gather. The bilinear gather broadens every point-source core by a constant tent of ~1/3 native pixel; FFT placement removes that systematic at the cost of wrap-around edge behaviour.
warnings: Experimental — validate against a bilinear run before adopting for production H₀ inference.

knobs.code_doc: Half-width (pixels) of a bounded prior on each point-image position around its detected position. null = an unbounded Normal(detected, 1 px).
knobs.curated_html: Bound the fitted position of every point image to ± this many pixels around its detected position: a TruncatedNormal(detected, 1 px) instead of the default unbounded Normal(detected, 1 px). It applies in GD, in the warm start and in sampling. Use it when a faint image sits next to bright extended light and could wander onto it. null (default) = unbounded.
warnings: A GD value exactly on the bound cannot be transferred to the sampler; the warm start then stops with an error. Widen the bound.

knobs.code_doc: Fit a constant sky level.
knobs.curated_html: Add a uniform sky-background component to the lens light with a wide, data-driven prior on its amplitude (site sky_amp). Use when the cutout has an unsubtracted sky pedestal — otherwise that flux gets absorbed into profile wings and biases the lens-light (and thus source) decomposition.

knobs.code_doc: Fix the sky at this value (model units) instead of fitting it.
knobs.curated_html:
Hold the uniform sky fixed instead of fitting it:

  • null (default): the sky amplitude sky_amp is a free parameter (when light.sky_background is on);
  • a number: the sky is fixed at that value (model units, per arcsec²) everywhere;
  • "refit": the sky is fitted by the full-frame lens-light refit and then held at that value in stage 3 and in sampling. On the full frame the refit separates sky and lens light; on the small modelling grid alone the sky trades off against an extended light envelope.
warnings: "refit" needs light.lens.refit.enabled; without the refit ALPACA warns and the sky stays free.

knobs.code_doc: 'unconvolved' (default): the sky is added after the PSF convolution; 'convolved': the sky is part of the convolved model (pre-0.5.3 behaviour).
knobs.curated_html: How the uniform sky enters the model: "unconvolved" (default) adds it after the PSF convolution, as a real sky pedestal; "convolved" (legacy) puts it inside the convolution, where the zero-padded convolution darkens the sky towards the frame edges.
Upper bound in Mpc (default 10000); must exceed low.
Lower bound in Mpc (default 500, must be positive). Lower it for low-redshift lenses; check boundary_flags.txt for D_dt at a bound.

Prior of the time-delay distance DΔt (Mpc): "uniform" (default) or "log_uniform" between low and high. The same distribution is the D_dt parameter of every model: GD, NumPyro NUTS, NIFTy, Nautilus and the prior-bound report all use it.

knobs.code_doc: ``"image_plane"`` (default since 0.6.0): one common source; the imaging centroids may differ from the lens-equation images by an image-plane Gaussian ``sigma_ast`` (mapped through each image's inverse-magnification matrix), the common source is the magnification-weighted mean, and all delays are evaluated for it (see :mod:`alpaca.models.astrometry`). Its likelihood is invariant under a mass-sheet transformation. Requires ``use_rayshoot_sys_error`` off and ``use_image_pos_offsets=False``. ``"source_plane"`` (the default up to 0.5.x, kept for comparisons): the back-traced source positions scatter around their mean with ``rayshoot_sigma`` (+ the optional free floor); a fixed source-plane width scales with the mass sheet, so this term carries artificial mass-sheet information.
knobs.curated_html:
How the measured positions of the point images constrain the mass model.

  • "image_plane" (default since 0.6.0; the shipped config.json and the tutorials write it explicitly): one common source. The measured positions may differ from the model's images by a Gaussian of width sigma_ast in the image plane (mapped through each image's inverse magnification matrix); the common source is the magnification-weighted mean, and all time delays are evaluated for it. This likelihood is invariant under a mass-sheet transformation. In GD stage 1, with rayshoot_against_source_pos: true, the common source is the centre of the analytic host model, i.e. the quasar sits on its host's nucleus.
  • "source_plane" (the default up to 0.5.x, kept for comparisons): the back-traced source positions scatter around their mean with rayshoot_sigma plus the optional free floor use_rayshoot_sys_error. A fixed source-plane width scales with a mass sheet, so this term carries artificial mass-sheet information.

"image_plane" requires use_rayshoot_sys_error off (its default null does that) and use_image_pos_offsets: false. A config without the key prints a one-line notice. Galaxy–galaxy lenses keep "image_plane": with fewer than two point images no astrometry term is built, in GD and in sampling.
warnings: Runs written before 0.6.0 (no config/alpaca_provenance.json) and legacy-layout configs are reloaded with the old defaults (source_plane, sigma_ast 0.003) for keys they omit, so an old run keeps its meaning. Write the key explicitly in every config.
sampler "nautilus" refuses image_plane astrometry (it has only the source-plane terms).

knobs.code_doc: Prior sigma (arcsec) on per-image position offsets. ``None`` (default) resolves to 0.01 arcsec (10 mas), the astrometric precision of PSF-fitted quasar images in HST/JWST data. (It used to resolve to one native pixel, ~31 mas for NIRCam SW, which let the mass model largely ignore the quasar positions and biased D_dt.)
knobs.curated_html: Gaussian prior width on each per-image offset. About one native pixel is the sensible scale — much larger and the offsets can absorb genuine mass-model misfit instead of centroid noise.

Mean of a Gaussian prior on the external convergence κext (truncated below 1). The default (mean 0, sigma 0) means no external convergence. κext enters the physical distance DΔtphys = DΔt / (λint (1 − κext)) and, with kinematics, the predicted velocity dispersions.

  • Without kinematics κext does not depend on the data: it is drawn per posterior sample into derived kappa_ext and D_dt_physical columns, and only when the distance is not blinded.
  • With kinematics and sigma > 0 it is a sampled parameter kin_kappa_ext, blinded like kin_lambda_int; sigma = 0 fixes it at the mean.

mean + 5·sigma must stay below 1. Set this or likelihood.kinematics.kappa_ext, not both.
Width of the κext prior (≥ 0; 0 = fixed at the mean). Not supported by the kinematics importance sampler (kinematics.importance_sample); use the joint likelihood.
Osipkov–Merritt ("om" / "gom") anisotropy: uniform prior range of aani, with anisotropy radius ra = aani θE.
Aperture solver: Sérsic deprojection nodes (default 64). Numerical.
Aperture solver: angular quadrature nodes (default 128). Numerical.

Distance normalisation of the dynamical model (Mpc). At fixed ds_over_dds it cancels for lensing-normalised power laws: it is NOT an external distance or H0 prior.
The distance ratio Ds/Dds of the lens. No default: it must be set when use_kinematics is on (validation stops otherwise). Compute it for your redshifts at a fiducial cosmology.

kin_center_dx/dy (east/north, arcsec) about the IFU origin

Aperture mode: 1σ error of observed_sigma (km/s), multiplied by covariance_scale.

knobs.code_doc: tracer_exclude: lens-light Sersic components (0-based) left OUT of the kinematic tracer (diagnostic)
Boost the noise map around detected point sources so they don't dominate the extended-source fit.
knobs.curated_html: Multiplicatively boost the noise map in a circle around each detected point source, so PSF-core residuals at the bright quasar images don't dominate the extended-source and lens-light fit. The factor decays linearly from f_max at the PS centre to 1.0 at the boost radius.

knobs.code_doc: Keyword arguments forwarded to ``boost_noise_around_point_sources``.
knobs.curated_html:
Parameters forwarded to boost_noise_around_point_sources:

  • f_max — maximum multiplicative noise factor at the PS centre (1.0 = no boost).
  • radius — boost radius in arcsec; null = auto from PS separations.
  • frac_min_sep — auto radius = fraction × minimum PS separation.
  • min_npix / max_npix — clamps on the auto radius, in pixels.

knobs.code_doc: Factor the noise is multiplied by at the centre of each point-source image when `noise_boost` is on; it falls linearly to 1 at the boost radius (overlapping regions keep the maximum).
Fraction of the minimum separation between point-source images used as the automatic boost radius (when `radius` is null). Default 0.4.
Upper limit (pixels) of the automatic boost radius. Default 6.
Lower limit (pixels) of the automatic boost radius. Default 2.5.
Boost radius in arcsec. `null` (default) derives it from the image configuration: `frac_min_sep` × the smallest pairwise image separation, clipped to [`min_npix`, `max_npix`] pixels.
Upper bound of the Uniform(0, b_max) prior on the sampled ``b``.
knobs.curated_html: Upper bound of the Uniform(0, b_max) prior on the sampled PSF-error amplitude b in σ²_eff = σ² + b²·ps_image². This is the anti-overfit cap: larger values let the likelihood down-weight the point-source regions more aggressively.
warnings: Check the FITTED b against this cap in the model summary — a b railing at b_max means the cap, not the data, is setting the point-source error budget, and the quoted fit quality inherits that choice.

knobs.code_doc: When/how the b term participates (validated in PipelineConfig): "joint"         - b free during GD and sampling (legacy). "post_gd_fixed" - b HELD AT 0 through GD stages 1-3; after stage 3 a 1-D exact fit of b at the frozen optimum (accounts for Poisson-noise underestimation at the PS cores); sampling runs with b FIXED at that value.
knobs.curated_html:
When the PSF-error amplitude b (σ2eff = σ² + b²·PS²) is fitted:

  • "post_gd_free" (default): b = 0 through GD stages 1–3, then an exact 1-D fit of b at the stage-3 optimum; sampling keeps b free, starting at that value;
  • "post_gd_fixed": the same, but sampling holds b at the fitted value;
  • "joint": b free in GD and in sampling (legacy).

Flux exponent p of the PSF-error term. 1 (default): σ2eff = σ² + b²·PS². p < 1: σ² + b²·PSpeak²·(PS/PSpeak)2p, which flattens the flux scaling so the PSF wings get relatively more weight reduction while the term stays confined to the point images. Nautilus supports only p = 1.

knobs.code_doc: Add a per-pixel variance term that scales with point-source flux: ``σ²_eff = σ² + b² · ps_image²`` where ``b`` is a sampled parameter.
knobs.curated_html: Add a per-pixel variance term scaling with point-source flux: σ²_eff = σ² + b² · ps_image², where b is a sampled Uniform(0, 0.1) parameter. A principled way to down-weight pixels where PSF-model errors dominate, letting the data infer how wrong the PSF is.

knobs.code_doc: If True, compare ray-traced positions to the sampled source position (``src_center_x/y``); if False, compare to the mean. With ``astrometry_mode="image_plane"`` and an analytic source (GD stage 1) the common source of the astrometry and of the delays is then the sampled source centre (quasar = host nucleus); pixelated sources have no centre and use the profiled common source.
knobs.curated_html: If true, ray-traced image positions are compared against the sampled source-light centre (src_center_x/y) — coupling the point-source astrometry to the extended-source model. If false, they are compared against their own mean (pure internal consistency, decoupled from the light centroid).

knobs.code_doc: Astrometric uncertainty floor (arcsec) for the ray-shooting term.
knobs.curated_html: Astrometric uncertainty floor for the ray-shooting term — smaller values make the consistency constraint tighter. 0.001–0.002 is typical for HST/JWST astrometry. If set too small, the term dominates the imaging likelihood and GD can stall in astrometry-driven local minima; the free systematic-error parameter (use_rayshoot_sys_error) is the safer way to let the data pick the floor.

knobs.code_doc: (min, max) range (arcsec) for the systematic-error parameter.
knobs.curated_html: (min, max) of the log-uniform prior on the ray-shooting systematic error. 5×10⁻⁵ arcsec = 0.05 mas is at the floor of instrument astrometry; 5×10⁻³ arcsec = 5 mas is very loose. Widen the upper end for systems with visible astrometric anomalies.

knobs.code_doc: Image-plane astrometric perturbation (arcsec) for ``"image_plane"``.
knobs.curated_html: Width (arcsec) of the image-plane Gaussian between measured and model image positions in astrometry_mode: "image_plane"; must be positive. Default 0.005 (5 mas), about the image-position scatter a smooth lens model leaves on a JWST quad; 0.003, the default up to 0.5.x, is too tight. Smaller values tie the mass model more tightly to the image positions.

knobs.code_doc: ``"source_plane"`` only (``"image_plane"`` always uses one source): evaluate ALL time delays for one source position -- the sampled ``src_center_x/y`` of an analytic source when ``rayshoot_against_source_pos`` is set, otherwise the magnification-weighted common source -- instead of each image's own back-traced position.
knobs.curated_html: Only for astrometry_mode: "source_plane" ("image_plane" always uses one source). true (default): all time delays are evaluated for ONE source position, the sampled centre of an analytic source when rayshoot_against_source_pos is set, otherwise the magnification-weighted common source. false uses each image's own back-traced position (ALPACA ≤ 0.5.0), which is physically inconsistent and adds first-order errors to the Fermat potential. Use false only to reproduce old runs.

knobs.code_doc: The measured delays (days), when they are not passed to ``run_pipeline`` directly (``run_alpaca.py`` reads them from here). Paste the published n-1 delays relative to one reference image:: "time_delays": { "convention": "t_X - t_Y", "delays": {"AB": [-9.0, 0.8], "AC": [-0.8, 0.7], "AD": [-13.8, 0.8]}, "covariance": "independent" } ``delays``: pair keys ``"XY"`` / ``"X-Y"`` with ``[value, error]`` or ``[value, +error, -error]`` (symmetrised); single labels ``"B"`` mean ``t_B - t_ref``. ``convention``: what the value of ``"XY"`` is, ``"t_X - t_Y"`` (default; COSMOGRAIL / H0LiCOW / TDCOSMO tables) or ``"t_Y - t_X"``. ``covariance``: ``"independent"`` (default; at most n-1 delays, each with its own error), or a matrix (days**2, rows in the order of ``delays``), a ``.npy``/``.txt``/``.csv``/``.json`` file or ``{"correlation": matrix}`` when the measurement provides one. Optional ``reference_image``. Every likelihood (GD/NUTS, NIFTy, Nautilus) uses the delays relative to the reference; see :mod:`alpaca.utils.time_delays`.
knobs.curated_html:
The measured time delays in days, pasted as published. null = no delays. The block has the keys delays, convention, covariance, and optionally pair_noise and reference_image:

"time_delays": {
  "convention": "t_X - t_Y",
  "delays": {"AB": [-9.0, 0.8], "AC": [-0.8, 0.7], "AD": [-13.8, 0.8]},
  "covariance": "independent"
}

Every likelihood (GD, NumPyro NUTS, NIFTy, Nautilus) uses the n−1 delays relative to the reference image. The run log prints the pair table, which image arrives later, and the delays and errors actually used: check it once for every lens. TIME_DELAYS in run_alpaca.py, when not None, overrides this block.
What the value of key "XY" means: "t_X - t_Y" (default; the convention of the COSMOGRAIL, H0LiCOW and TDCOSMO tables) or "t_Y - t_X". A positive tX − tY means that X arrives after Y.

• "independent" (default): each listed delay has its own error; at most n−1 delays without a cycle;
  • "shared_curves": every pair is measured from two light curves; a timing error per curve is fitted to the published pair errors, so pairs that share an image are correlated. Needs a redundant table (each image in at least two pairs, with a triangle), e.g. all six pairs of a quad;
  • a matrix: the covariance of the listed delays in days², rows in the order of delays; or the path of a .npy / .txt / .csv / .json file holding it;
  • {"correlation": R}: a correlation matrix, combined with the listed errors.

Redundant tables are combined exactly into the n−1 delays relative to the reference. With "shared_curves" the listed delays must close (tXY + tYZ = tXZ) to within 1.5 × the largest pair error; a larger violation is a sign or label error and stops the run (add pair_noise for measured pairs that genuinely do not close).

The delays, keyed by image pair, "AB" or "A-B"; each value is [value, σ] or [value, +σ, −σ] (asymmetric errors are symmetrised, with a note in the log). The labels are the run's image labels (IMAGE_POSITIONS in run_alpaca.py, or multiband.image_positions).

Give the n−1 independent delays relative to one image (three for a quad). With covariance: "independent" a redundant table (e.g. all six pairs of a quad) is refused, because the pairs share light curves; use "shared_curves" or a matrix for such tables.

Legacy form (ALPACA ≤ 0.5.1), still accepted: single labels, {"B": [t_B − t_ref, σ], …}. Its sign is the opposite of the published ΔtAB = tA − tB.
warnings: Paste COSMOGRAIL / H0LiCOW / TDCOSMO delays with their published signs: the default convention "t_X - t_Y" is theirs. Do not flip them.

knobs.curated_html: An independent per-pair error (days) on top of the per-curve timing errors; only with covariance: "shared_curves". Must be smaller than every listed pair error.
Label of the image the delays are taken relative to (the anchor of the likelihood). Overrides REFERENCE_IMAGE in run_alpaca.py. With a full covariance the likelihood does not depend on this choice.

knobs.code_doc: Add per-image position offsets (TD + rayshoot terms only). Default False; when enabled, their prior width is ``image_pos_offset_sigma``.
knobs.curated_html: Sample per-image position offsets offset_{x,y}_image_{i} applied in the time-delay and ray-shooting terms — accounting for astrometric errors in the detected image centroids without moving the imaging-likelihood positions. One x/y pair per point-source image.
warnings: Must be false with astrometry_mode "image_plane".

knobs.code_doc: Stellar kinematics (off by default; see KinematicsConfig).
knobs.curated_html: Add a stellar-kinematics likelihood (off by default; nothing else changes while it is off), configured in likelihood.kinematics: one aperture velocity dispersion (mode: "aperture", spherical Jeans) or binned IFU Vrms (mode: "resolved", spherical Jeans or axisymmetric JAM). Requires kinematics.ds_over_dds and Sérsic lens-light components, which are the kinematic tracer. The internal mass-sheet parameter λint is sampled by default and is always blinded when blinding is on.

knobs.code_doc: Add a penalty for scatter in ray-traced source positions.
knobs.curated_html: Add a penalty for scatter among the ray-traced source positions of the different point-source images — all images must trace back to the same source point. This is the imaging counterpart of the classical point-source astrometric likelihood and substantially tightens the mass model near the images.
warnings: Force-disabled when light.point_sources.enabled=false (no images to back-project).

knobs.code_doc: Sample a free systematic-error parameter for ray-shooting (``"source_plane"`` only). ``None`` (default) resolves to ``True`` for ``"source_plane"`` (its historical default) and ``False`` for ``"image_plane"``, which replaces the floor by ``sigma_ast``.
knobs.curated_html: Sample a free systematic floor (arcsec, within rayshoot_sys_error_range) added to rayshoot_sigma in the source-plane astrometry. null (default) resolves to true for astrometry_mode: "source_plane" (its historical default) and false for "image_plane", where sigma_ast replaces the floor. true together with "image_plane" is refused.

knobs.code_doc: Include the time-delay likelihood term.
knobs.curated_html:
Include the time-delay likelihood: the model's delays (Fermat-potential differences × DΔt) against the measured delays in likelihood.time_delays. true makes the run a DΔt / H0 inference; false for imaging-only fits.

run_alpaca.py stops with an error when this is true, point sources are on and no delays are given. It is switched off automatically in galaxy–galaxy mode.

knobs.code_doc: How the deflection is evaluated. ``"series"`` : closed-form homoeoid/Legendre series (:mod:`alpaca.models.bpl_series`) — same physics, more accurate than the quadrature at every axis ratio tested and ~3x cheaper per call. ``"quadrature"``: the original two-panel Gauss-Legendre evaluation.
knobs.curated_html: How the broken-power-law deflection is evaluated: "series" (default), a closed-form homoeoid / Legendre series, more accurate and about 3× cheaper than the quadrature; "quadrature", the original two-panel Gauss–Legendre evaluation.

knobs.code_doc: ``{"loc", "scale", "low", "high"}`` for a TruncatedNormal, the same shape as the EPL's ``gamma_prior``. The default is deliberately WIDER than the EPL default (scale 0.3 vs 0.15): a broken profile splits the single well-constrained lensing slope between two parameters, so each is individually less constrained and a tight prior would just re-impose the EPL answer.
knobs.curated_html: TruncatedNormal prior on the INNER slope (same shape as the EPL's gamma_prior; bpl.gamma_out is the outer twin). Deliberately WIDER than the EPL default (scale 0.3 vs 0.15): a broken profile splits the single well-constrained lensing slope between two parameters, and a tight prior would just re-impose the EPL answer.

knobs.code_doc: Upper truncation of the γ_in prior (default 2.7).

Centre of the TruncatedNormal prior on the INNER slope γ_in of the broken power law (default 2.0). The BPL priors are deliberately wider than the EPL's: the single, well-constrained lensing slope is split between two parameters.
Lower truncation of the γ_in prior (default 1.3).
Width of the TruncatedNormal prior on γ_in (default 0.3; the EPL uses 0.15).

``{"loc", "scale", "low", "high"}`` for a TruncatedNormal, the same shape as the EPL's ``gamma_prior``. The default is deliberately WIDER than the EPL default (scale 0.3 vs 0.15): a broken profile splits the single well-constrained lensing slope between two parameters, so each is individually less constrained and a tight prior would just re-impose the EPL answer.
knobs.curated_html: TruncatedNormal prior on the OUTER slope — the twin of mass.main.bpl.gamma_in (see that entry for why the priors are deliberately wide). Sub-keys: loc/scale are the Normal centre and width, low/high the truncation bounds.

knobs.code_doc: Upper truncation of the γ_out prior (default 2.7).
Centre of the TruncatedNormal prior on the OUTER slope γ_out (default 2.0). γ_in = γ_out reproduces the EPL exactly.
Lower truncation of the γ_out prior (default 1.3).
Width of the γ_out prior (default 0.3).

Gauss-Legendre nodes PER PANEL (two panels, split at the break) for the deflection and the potential. See :mod:`alpaca.models.mass_profiles` — 24/28 gives ~1e-13 relative accuracy for a round-to-mildly-flattened deflector and stays below 1e-6 down to q ~ 0.5. Lower only if profiling says so. Used for the potential always, and for the deflection only when ``deflection == "quadrature"``.
knobs.curated_html: Gauss-Legendre nodes PER PANEL (two panels, split analytically at the break) for the BPL deflection; n_quad_potential (default 28) is the potential's counterpart. 24 reproduces the analytic EPL to ~1e-13 at γ=2 (where the endpoint substitution makes the quadrature exact) and stays below 1e-6 relative down to q~0.55. Lower only if profiling says so.

knobs.code_doc: Gauss-Legendre nodes PER PANEL (two panels, split at the break) for the deflection and the potential. See :mod:`alpaca.models.mass_profiles` — 24/28 gives ~1e-13 relative accuracy for a round-to-mildly-flattened deflector and stays below 1e-6 down to q ~ 0.5. Lower only if profiling says so. Used for the potential always, and for the deflection only when ``deflection == "quadrature"``.
Terms of each series (the two EPL pieces and the core term). They converge like ((1-q)/(1+q))^n; 40 keeps the error below 1e-13" for q >= 0.3 and below the quadrature's everywhere down to q = 0.2.
``[low, high]`` bounds of the Uniform prior on ``r_break/theta_E``.
knobs.curated_html: Uniform prior bounds on the break radius in units of θE (site lens_r_break_frac). Tying the break to θ_E keeps it inside the annulus the arcs actually constrain for every sample, instead of letting the chain wander into a regime where the second slope is unconstrained.

knobs.code_doc: Width [arcsec] of the Normal prior of the mass centre around the (detected / given) lens-light centre. None = mode default: 0.3" when point sources anchor the mass (quasar mode), 0.05" without them (galaxy-galaxy mode), where nothing else ties the mass to the lens and multistarts otherwise settle on a small-theta_E "lens" on an arc image.
knobs.curated_html: Width (arcsec) of the Normal prior of the mass centre around the lens-light centre. null (default) chooses by mode: 0.3″ when point images anchor the mass (quasars), 0.05″ without them (galaxy–galaxy), where nothing else ties the mass to the lens galaxy and a multistart could otherwise place a small "lens" on an arc.

Add a free external flexion to the main deflector: the cubic term of an external lens potential, centred on the lens, one order beyond the external shear. It absorbs the gradient of the environment's convergence and shear across the lens. Four sampled parameters lens_flex_g1 … lens_flex_g4 (1/arcsec), each TruncatedNormal(0, sigma; ±max). Off by default.
Truncation of each flexion component at ±max (1/arcsec, default 0.5). A component at this bound is a warning sign, as for any prior bound.
Width of the TruncatedNormal prior of each flexion component (1/arcsec, default 0.05). Must be positive.

knobs.code_doc: If True use the ELLIPTICAL multipoles of Paugnat & Gilman (2025) (lenstronomy's ``MULTIPOLE_ELL``, :class:`alpaca.models.multipole_ell.MultipoleEllCS`) instead of the default circular ones: the perturbation then deforms the main deflector's own elliptical isodensity contours, sharing its axis ratio and position angle, and the phase is measured from its major axis. Only ``m = 1, 3, 4`` are implemented. Default False (the circular :class:`MultipoleCS`, unchanged behaviour).
Multipole orders to include, e.g. ``[1, 3, 4]``. Empty (default) = no multipoles, i.e. the historical EPL+SHEAR model. ``m = 2`` is NOT recommended: it is degenerate with the EPL ellipticity.
knobs.curated_html:
Angular multipole orders added to the main deflector, e.g. [3, 4]. Each order m adds the convergence κ_m = a_m·cos[m(φ−φ_m)]/(2r) and TWO sampled sites, the Cartesian pair lens_a{m}_cos/lens_a{m}_sin (single-valued and smooth through zero — the polar (a_m, φ_m) pair is 2m-fold multimodal and singular exactly at the a_m=0 null-test point). All amplitudes zero = the EPL, bit-for-bit.

m=4 is boxy/discy — the mode with real photometric backing (a₄/a ~ 1–2% in ellipticals). m=3 is the triangular mode. m=1 is supported (it needs a special r·ln r potential — the scale-free form divides by zero) but see the warning.

knobs.code_doc: Reference radius (arcsec) in the ``m = 1`` potential ``psi = (1/2) r ln(r/r_ref) C(phi)``. Changing it only adds a CONSTANT deflection (degenerate with the source position) and does not touch the convergence; it is fixed rather than sampled so the ``m = 1`` amplitudes stay well conditioned. Default 1.0" ~ theta_E.
knobs.curated_html: Reference radius (arcsec) in the m=1 potential ψ₁ = ½·r·ln(r/r_ref)·C(φ). Changing it only adds a CONSTANT deflection — exactly degenerate with a source-plane shift, leaving the convergence untouched — so it is held fixed (~θ_E) rather than sampled. Ignored without m=1.

knobs.code_doc: Width of the zero-mean Normal prior on each Cartesian amplitude, in arcsec. A dict maps order -> sigma (keys may be ints or strings), any missing order falling back to ``sigma_default``. Scale intuition: the convergence perturbation is ``kappa_m = a_m cos(m(phi-phi_m)) / (2 r)``, so ``a_m / theta_E`` is the usual dimensionless multipole strength. Real ellipticals have ``a_4/a ~ 0.01-0.02``; for a ``theta_E ~ 1"`` lens the default ``sigma = 0.02"`` is a weakly informative ~1.7% prior that still lets the data push to ~5% amplitudes.
knobs.curated_html: Width (arcsec) of the zero-mean Normal prior on each Cartesian amplitude; a dict maps order → σ with sigma_default as fallback. The example uses null, so every configured order delegates to sigma_default = 0.02. Scale intuition: a_m/θ_E is the usual dimensionless strength; real ellipticals sit at 0.01–0.02, so σ=0.02" (~2% of a typical θ_E) is weakly informative and lets the data push to ~5%.

knobs.code_doc: Fallback width when ``sigma`` is a dict without that order.
knobs.curated_html: Fallback prior width used for any multipole order not listed when multipoles.sigma is a per-order dict (or when it is null).

knobs.code_doc: Radial profile of the main deflector. ``"epl"`` (default) is the historical elliptical power law with a single ``lens_gamma``; ``"bpl"`` is the elliptical broken power law (see :class:`BrokenPowerLawConfig`).
knobs.curated_html:
Radial mass profile of the main deflector.

  • "EPL+Shear" — elliptical power law + external shear, one slope lens_gamma. The historical model (legacy alias "epl").
  • "BPL+Shear" — elliptical broken power law + external shear (legacy alias "bpl"): slope gamma_in inside a break radius, gamma_out outside. Samples lens_gamma_in, lens_gamma_out, lens_r_break_frac and removes lens_gamma. Reduces to the EPL exactly at gamma_in = gamma_out (verified to ~1e-13), and θE keeps its EPL meaning (mean convergence 1 inside θE) so the two models are directly comparable.

The BPL has no closed-form deflection — it is evaluated by desingularised Gauss-Legendre quadrature (Keeton 2001), costing ~×1.8 per gradient.

The profile string selects the RADIAL model only — angular structure is added independently via mass.main.multipoles.orders (combinable with either profile), and the external shear is always part of the model.

knobs.code_doc: {center, sigma} in arcsec: TruncatedNormal prior on the Einstein radius. Required for galaxy-galaxy lenses.
knobs.curated_html: Optional prior on the main-lens Einstein radius, {"center": θ, "sigma": σ} in arcsec: a TruncatedNormal within the physical bounds. null keeps the wide uniform prior set by the detected image positions (quasars). Only center and sigma are accepted.
warnings: Galaxy–galaxy lenses: always set it (e.g. the ring radius, σ ≈ 0.1–0.2″). Without point images ALPACA takes the θE scale, the arc annulus and the R_eff bounds from theta_E_prior.center and warns when it is missing; without it θE can run to about twice the true value.

knobs.curated_html: Fiducial H₀ for the multi-plane distance-ratio (η) matrix and the fiducial time-delay distance used to rescale multi-plane arrival times onto the sampled D_dt. Distance ratios are exactly H₀-independent, so this choice does not bias the H₀ inference — it is the standard treatment.
Fiducial matter density for the multi-plane distance ratios. The dependence of the ratios on Ω_m is weak; 0.3 is the conventional choice.

knobs.code_doc: Explicit whitelist / blacklist of catalog ids.
knobs.curated_html: Explicit blacklist of catalog ids to drop regardless of other filters. null = no blacklist.

knobs.code_doc: Explicit whitelist / blacklist of catalog ids.
knobs.curated_html: Explicit whitelist of catalog ids. When set, only these perturbers are modelled (still subject to the flexion cut). null = no whitelist.

knobs.code_doc: Drop catalog perturbers below this flexion shift. None keeps all.
knobs.curated_html: Drop catalog perturbers whose flexion shift is below this threshold. The flexion shift is the standard importance ranking for line-of-sight structure — a threshold around 10⁻⁴ arcsec keeps only perturbers that measurably affect the model.

knobs.code_doc: "auto" = honest plane assignment (multi-plane when needed); "single_plane" = force ALL perturbers into the main lens plane (classic approximation; keeps the single-plane forward model).
knobs.curated_html: "auto" gives honest plane assignment: perturbers within z_tolerance of the lens redshift join the main plane as ordinary profiles; the rest get their own fore-/background planes, switching to multi-plane ray tracing with distance ratios fixed at the fiducial cosmology and arrival times rescaled by the sampled D_dt. "single_plane" forces all perturbers into the main lens plane — the classic approximation that keeps the cheaper single-plane forward model.

knobs.code_doc: Perturber catalog JSON (target block + perturbers list, as written by the perturber-finder tool). Per-dataset — usually set via PERTURBERS_PATH in run_alpaca.py.
knobs.curated_html:
The perturber catalogue (JSON: a target block and a list of perturbers; format in the guide, Perturbers). null = no perturbers: the model is then exactly the single-plane pipeline. Each perturber gets the mass profile declared in its entry, and optionally a light model; perturbers outside z_tolerance of the lens redshift get their own planes, which switches the forward model to multi-plane lensing.

PERTURBERS_PATH in run_alpaca.py, when not None, overrides this. Relative paths are relative to the working directory; use absolute paths.
warnings: A perturber's light is modelled only when its catalogue entry has a lens_light block. Mask every other galaxy in data.likelihood_mask_path, or its flux biases the fit.

knobs.code_doc: Freeze perturber centers at the catalog positions (no position latents; only theta_E is sampled).
knobs.curated_html: Freeze perturber centres at the catalog positions — no position latents; only θ_E stays free. Cuts two latents per perturber; use when the catalog astrometry is trustworthy and the perturbers are weak.

knobs.code_doc: Normal prior width (arcsec) on each perturber center, around the catalog position.
knobs.curated_html: Normal prior width on each perturber centre around its catalog position (converted into the model frame). Wide enough to absorb astrometric frame offsets; the overlay plot in 01_input/ shows the anchors so you can verify the conversion.

knobs.code_doc: theta_E prior is Uniform(0, factor * theta_E_catalog).
knobs.curated_html: Each perturber's Einstein radius gets a Uniform(0, factor × θ_E,catalog) prior. The factor absorbs catalog mass uncertainties; 3× is generous without letting a perturber grow into a second main deflector.

knobs.code_doc: Redshift window around z_lens for main-plane membership.
knobs.curated_html: Redshift window around the lens: perturbers with |z − z_lens| ≤ z_tolerance are placed in the main lens plane. Must be ≥ 0 (validated). Widening it trades multi-plane fidelity for a simpler, faster model.

  "reference_band": "F150W",
  "bands": {"F150W": {"data_dir": "data/F150W"},
            "F356W": {"data_dir": "data/F356W",

}

With likelihood.use_kinematics: the band whose lens light is the kinematic tracer (default: the reference band). Override one group after the preset, e.g. "sharing": {"preset": "lensing", "lens_light_shape": "shared"}. Groups: mass, perturber_mass, cosmology, kinematics, image_positions, ps_amplitudes, lens_light_shape, lens_light_amplitude, sky, source, perturber_light, noise_model, psf; each "shared" or "per_band". Parameters that match no group stay per band and are listed in the log. The source is always per band in this version.

Which parameter groups are common to all bands ("shared": one value, sampled once with the reference band's prior) and which are free per band ("per_band", named <band>/<parameter>):

  • "lensing" (default): mass, perturber mass, DΔt, image positions and kinematic nuisances shared; every photometric group per band;
  • "achromatic_lens_light": lensing + one lens-light geometry for all bands (amplitudes per band);
  • "independent": nothing shared, one separate lens per band, as a consistency check.
