knobs.curated_html: Per-pixel 1σ map of the input PSF (.npy / .npz / FITS), on the grid of the seed's background. In joint mode with psf.joint.priors.background.type: "error_map" it sets the prior width of every free PSF pixel: about 1–10 % of the kernel. Too loose and the PSF fits noise around bright images; too tight and it cannot correct the seed. PSF_ERROR_MAP_PATH in run_alpaca.py, when not None, overrides it.

knobs.code_doc: How a PSF error map on a different grid is matched to the PSF prior grid: `"none"` (default) requires the map on exactly that grid and raises an error otherwise; `"bilinear"` interpolates it (legacy behaviour, opt-in). Supplying the map on the right grid (STARRED, `high_res=True`, same stamp) is the clean option.

Supersampling factor of the INPUT PSF relative to the data pixel grid. 1 = PSF at data resolution. >1 = PSF is N× finer than the data pixels (e.g. a JWST PSF provided at 5× oversampling needs ``oversample=5``). When >1, Herculens enables supersampled convolution and keeps the PSF at its native finer resolution through the forward model.
knobs.curated_html: Supersampling factor of the PSF file relative to the image pixels: 1 = the PSF is sampled like the data; N > 1 = N× finer (usually 3). With N > 1 the model is convolved at the fine resolution. PSF_OVERSAMPLE in run_alpaca.py, when not None, overrides it.

knobs.code_doc: Size of the STARRED per-source stamps in native data pixels. Must be odd; even values are bumped up by 1. ``"auto"`` (default) uses the native-resolution PSF size (``psf_kernel.shape[0] // psf.input.oversample``). Shrinking this (e.g. to 61–81) restricts STARRED's fit to the signal-carrying core of the PSF and avoids letting the background-grid absorb noise from the wings. Note that this also shrinks the reconstructed PSF kernel returned to the rest of the pipeline to ``cutout_size_pix`` native pixels (``cutout_size_pix * starred_oversample`` high-res pixels).
knobs.curated_html: Size of the STARRED per-source stamps in native pixels. Must be odd (even values are bumped up by 1); "auto" uses the native-resolution PSF size (kernel_size // psf.input.oversample). Shrinking to 61–81 restricts the fit to the signal-carrying PSF core and stops the background grid from absorbing wing noise.

knobs.code_doc: Upper bound of the ``Uniform(0, b_max)`` prior on ``psf_error_b`` **during the PSF reconstruction stage only**. ``None`` uses the ProbModel default (0.1). Raising it (e.g. to 0.3–0.5) gives the likelihood more room to absorb PSF mis-modelling in the early iterations when the initial PSF is very approximate. Automatically restored before multistart MAP + sampling. Only meaningful when the error map is active during the PSF stage (via ``enabled`` here or the global ``likelihood.noise_model.use_psf_error_map``).
knobs.curated_html: Upper bound of the Uniform(0, b_max) prior on psf_error_b during the reconstruction stage only. Raising it to 0.3–0.5 gives the likelihood more room to absorb PSF mis-modelling in early iterations when the initial PSF is crude. Restored before multistart + sampling.
warnings: Only meaningful when the error map is active during the PSF stage — via enabled=true here or the global likelihood.noise_model.use_psf_error_map.

knobs.code_doc: If True, enables Herculens' PSF error map (a PSF-shaped noise inflation ``sigma_eff² = sigma² + b² * ps_image²`` with ``b`` sampled on ``Uniform(0, b_max)``) **only for the PSF reconstruction stage**. Down-weights point-source cores during the internal GD so the lens/source/lens-light fit isn't starved by PSF mis-modelling leverage — giving STARRED cleaner model-subtracted stamps. Automatically reverts before multistart MAP and posterior sampling, which then see the user's global ``likelihood.noise_model.use_psf_error_map`` setting unchanged. Independent of that global flag: if both are True, this one is a no-op (PSF stage already has the error map).
knobs.curated_html: Enable Herculens' PSF error map (σ²_eff = σ² + b² · ps_image², b ~ Uniform(0, b_max)) only during the PSF reconstruction stage. Down-weights point-source cores in the internal GD so the lens/source/lens-light fit isn't starved by PSF-mismodelling leverage, giving STARRED cleaner model-subtracted stamps. Automatically reverted before multistart MAP and sampling, which see the global likelihood.noise_model.use_psf_error_map unchanged.
warnings: If the global use_psf_error_map is already true, this flag is a no-op — the PSF stage already has the error map.

knobs.code_doc: Mask other detected peaks when reconstructing each PS.
knobs.curated_html: When fitting each point source in STARRED, mask the other detected peaks so a neighbouring image's flux doesn't contaminate the stamp. Essential for small-separation quads.

knobs.code_doc: Radius (pixels) of the mask around other peaks.
knobs.curated_html: Radius of the mask placed over each contaminant peak. Should comfortably cover the neighbour's PSF core without eating the stamp being fitted.

knobs.code_doc: Window-function shape for the contaminant-PS masks fed to STARRED. ``"cosine"`` (default) applies a raised-cosine taper outside ``radius_pix`` over a width ``smoothing_width_pix``, suppressing the Fourier-domain ringing that a hard 0/1 cut would inject into the PSF reconstruction. ``"hard"`` reproduces the legacy 0/1 binary mask. ``"gaussian"`` uses ``1 - exp(-r^2 / (2 * R^2))`` with ``R = radius_pix``.
knobs.curated_html: Window shape of the contaminant masks fed to STARRED. "cosine" applies a raised-cosine taper outside radius_pix over smoothing_width_pix, suppressing the Fourier-domain ringing a hard 0/1 edge injects into the reconstruction. "hard" reproduces the legacy binary mask; "gaussian" uses 1 − exp(−r²/2R²) with R = radius_pix.

knobs.code_doc: Width (pixels) of the cosine taper. Ignored when ``smoothing != "cosine"``.
knobs.curated_html: Width of the raised-cosine taper. Ignored unless smoothing="cosine". Must be non-negative (validated).

knobs.code_doc: Number of iterative PSF refinement passes.
knobs.curated_html: Number of outer refinement passes: fit lens model → subtract extended light → re-fit PSF on the cleaned point sources → repeat. Two passes usually converge; more help when the initial PSF is very approximate.

knobs.code_doc: Random starts for multi-start optimization per iteration.
knobs.curated_html: Random starts for the internal lens-modelling multi-start inside each PSF iteration. Higher = more robust extended-light subtraction (and thus cleaner PSF stamps), slower.

knobs.code_doc: Clip pixels below ``-negative_sigma_clip * σ`` in the reconstructed PSF. ``None`` disables clipping.
knobs.curated_html: Clip reconstructed PSF pixels below −N × σ — masking negative reconstruction artefacts that would imprint dark rings around every point source. null disables clipping.

knobs.code_doc: Parallelize multi-start evaluations across devices.
knobs.curated_html: Parallelize the multi-start evaluations across available devices (GPUs). Disable only for debugging or on memory-starved single-GPU nodes.

knobs.code_doc: Rotation augmentation mode for STARRED.
knobs.curated_html: Rotation augmentation inside STARRED: "90" adds a 90°-rotated copy of each stamp, "all" every 90° rotation. Augmentation suppresses detector-frame systematics at the cost of imprinting rotational symmetry on the kernel — leave "none" for PSFs with strong diffraction spikes.

knobs.code_doc: Supersampling factor inside STARRED. ``None`` (default) inherits ``psf.input.oversample`` so the reconstruction works on the same grid as the input PSF.
knobs.curated_html: Internal supersampling factor of the STARRED reconstruction grid. The reconstructed kernel is returned at this resolution relative to native pixels.

knobs.code_doc: Convolution backend for the live kernel ("fft").
knobs.curated_html: Convolution backend for the live kernel. "fft" is the supported production choice; direct convolution is orders of magnitude slower for typical kernel sizes.

knobs.code_doc: Which PSF blocks are free GD latents.
knobs.curated_html: Which PSF blocks become free GD latents. "moffat" frees the analytic core (FWHM, β, ellipticity C, angle φ); "background" frees the STARRED pixel grid that carries diffraction structure and wings. Freeing both gives the most faithful kernel but adds the full grid as latents — the background prior configuration below then matters a lot.

knobs.code_doc: Supersampling factor of the live joint kernel (STARRED grid). Fallback when the seed does not record its own ``upsampling_factor``. ``None`` (default) inherits ``psf.input.oversample`` — the joint kernel lives on the same grid as the input PSF.
knobs.curated_html: Supersampling factor of the live joint kernel (the STARRED grid). Used as a fallback when the seed file does not record its own upsampling_factor — a seed that records it wins.

knobs.code_doc: Global scale on the measured error map (``type == "error_map"``).
knobs.curated_html: Global scale on the measured error map in the "error_map" recipe. 1.0 trusts the map as-is; > 1 inflates the prior widths if the map is known to be optimistic (e.g. it omits systematic terms).

knobs.code_doc: Numerical floor added to the per-pixel width (heuristic and error_map recipes). ``None`` -> 5% of the seed background std.
knobs.curated_html: Numerical floor added to the per-pixel width (heuristic and error_map recipes). Guards against σᵢ → 0 in the zero-error wings, which would freeze those pixels and can condition the optimisation badly. null uses 5% of the seed background's standard deviation.

knobs.code_doc: Non-centered reparametrization of the free background grid (b = seed + sigma*z, z~N(0,1)). Identical prior, well-conditioned geometry for tiny sigma. Set False for the original centered behaviour.
knobs.curated_html: Non-centered reparametrization of the free background grid: b = seed + σ·z with z ~ N(0,1) as the latent. The prior is identical, but the geometry is far better conditioned when σ is tiny (as it is with a measured error map) — recommended whenever the background is free.

knobs.code_doc: Relative width for the heuristic recipe.
knobs.curated_html: Relative width for the "heuristic" recipe: σᵢ = rel × |seedᵢ| + floor. Larger values let bright background pixels move more.

knobs.code_doc: Global scalar width; required when ``type == "scalar"``.
knobs.curated_html: Global scalar width for the "scalar" recipe — one σ for every background pixel.

knobs.code_doc: Space the error-map prior acts in: ``"background"`` (legacy: width on the bg latent) or ``"kernel"`` (Gaussian prior on the full PSF kernel via a factor — the physically correct space; no deconvolution of the narrow->full convolution needed).
knobs.curated_html: Space the error-map prior acts in. "kernel" places a Gaussian prior on the full PSF kernel via a likelihood factor — the physically correct space, since the error map measures kernel uncertainty (and no deconvolution of the narrow→full convolution is needed). "background" is the legacy behaviour: the width is applied directly to the background latent.

knobs.code_doc: Which prior-width recipe to use (see above).
knobs.curated_html:
Recipe for the per-pixel prior width on the free STARRED background grid (only consulted when "background" is in psf.joint.free):

  • "heuristic" — σᵢ = rel × |seedᵢ| + floor: freedom proportional to the seed's own structure.
  • "error_map" — σᵢ = sqrt((α × errmapᵢ)² + floor²): the measured uncertainty of the seed PSF, read from psf.input.error_map_path. The physically motivated choice when you have an empirical error map.
  • "scalar" — one global σ for every pixel.

knobs.code_doc: Absolute Normal(0, sigma) prior for the Moffat angle phi (whose seed is ~0).
knobs.curated_html: Absolute Normal(0, σ) prior on the Moffat position angle φ, whose seed value is ~0 (a relative width would collapse to zero there).

knobs.code_doc: Moffat priors: Normal(seed, rel*|seed|) for fwhm/beta/C.
knobs.curated_html: Relative prior width on the Moffat core parameters: Normal(seed, rel × |seed|) for FWHM, β and the ellipticity parameter C. 0.1 = 10% freedom around the seed — enough to correct a slightly wrong STARRED fit while anchoring the core against source–PSF degeneracy.
Starlet regularization strength on the highest-frequency scale — the main defence against the background grid absorbing pixel noise.

Penalty on negative kernel pixels. The shipped value (10⁶) makes positivity effectively a hard constraint; the small dataclass default only nudges. Negative PSF pixels imprint dark rings around every point source, so a strong positivity term is usually right.
STARRED-style starlet regularization strength on the coarse wavelet scales of the live kernel — suppresses smooth spurious structure the imaging likelihood can't constrain.
warnings: The lambdas here are unnormalised (no star noise-map W), so values tuned inside STARRED/JWSTPSF do not transfer 1:1 — calibrate empirically on your data.

knobs.code_doc: Path to the JWSTPSF/STARRED seed (kwargs_moffat + kwargs_background). Required in joint mode.
knobs.curated_html: The STARRED seed (.npz with kwargs_moffat, the analytic core, and kwargs_background, the pixel grid) from a PSF fit to field stars. Required in joint mode: the live PSF is built from this seed, not from the kernel file, so the two must agree (the seed's full PSF reproduces the kernel to better than 1 % of the peak). PSF_STARRED_KWARGS_PATH in run_alpaca.py, when not None, overrides it.

knobs.code_doc: When True, allow ``psf.input.oversample > 1`` in joint mode so the bright point-source cores are rendered with a LIVE supersampled (high-res) joint PSF kernel (Moffat fit at os-resolution; STARRED background built on the os grid). Extended light stays on the static supersampled SubgridKernelConvolution path (seed HR kernel). Requires ``data.source_oversample == psf.input.oversample``. Set False for the native-only joint behaviour.
knobs.curated_html: Allow psf.input.oversample > 1 in joint mode: bright point-source cores are rendered with a live supersampled joint kernel (Moffat evaluated at the oversampled resolution; STARRED background built on the oversampled grid), while extended light stays on the static supersampled convolution path using the seed high-res kernel. Set this to false for native-resolution-only joint behaviour.

The single source of truth for how the PSF is treated:

  • "fixed" — trust the PSF you provide; no reconstruction at all. Only the psf.input section matters.
  • "iterative" — iteratively reconstruct the PSF with STARRED before the main gradient descent (settings under psf.iterative).
  • "joint" — fit the PSF (Moffat core + optional background grid) jointly with the lens model during gradient descent, seeded from a STARRED/JWSTPSF fit (settings under psf.joint).

The subsection not matching the mode is ignored; if an ignored section differs from its defaults, a notice is printed so a stale section can't silently mislead. The legacy layout (run_psf, mode="joint_gd", flat psf.joint_* keys) is auto-upgraded with a deprecation notice.

knobs.code_doc: Run the gradient-descent stages (MAP).
knobs.curated_html: Run the multi-start gradient-descent MAP stage (03_multistart/). Nearly always true — the MAP point seeds the sampler, defines the signal-derived arc mask, and (in joint PSF mode) carries the PSF fit. Set false only to start sampling directly from prior means or from a previous run's best fit.

knobs.code_doc: Directory for all outputs of this run. A new directory per model variant: re-running into an existing directory resumes it. A `{date}` placeholder is replaced by the start time; `null` = `./results/run_{date}/`. `--output` on the command line overrides it.
knobs.curated_html: Directory for all outputs of this run (inputs as figures, multistart, sampling, posterior, timing). The token {date} is replaced by a YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM timestamp. With run_alpaca.py an omitted key gives ./results/run_{date}/; --output DIR overrides the config. Use one directory per model variant: re-running a config into an existing directory resumes it.
warnings: Resume keys off the stage folders inside output_dir: reuse the same directory (no {date} token) when a rerun should skip finished stages, and never reuse one directory for another variant.

knobs.code_doc: Seed for every random choice (multistart draws, perturbations, sampler).
knobs.curated_html: Master PRNG seed, propagated to every stochastic component: multi-start initial positions, Adam/L-BFGS randomness, sampler chains, posterior subsampling. Fixing it makes runs bit-reproducible on the same hardware/software stack; change it to probe run-to-run scatter of the multistart.

knobs.code_doc: Skip GD and load a previous MAP (for sampling only).
knobs.curated_html: Only consulted when run.multistart=false: if true, load the best-fit parameters from a previous run's 03_multistart/ directory and use them as the sampling start point; if false, start from prior means.
warnings: The loaded best fit must come from a compatible model. The staged flow fingerprints the configuration and ALPACA's code, and recomputes (archiving the old folder as stage…stale-<time>) every stage whose objective changed, e.g. after new time delays.

knobs.code_doc: Folder of the previous 03_multistart to load when resuming.
knobs.curated_html: Explicit path to a previous run's 03_multistart/ directory. When null, the path is derived from output_dir. Only used when resume_from_previous=true.

knobs.code_doc: Run posterior sampling after the GD stages.
knobs.curated_html: Run posterior sampling (NUTS / Nautilus / NIFTy) after gradient descent. Disable to stop after the MAP stage — useful for quick model checks, arc-mask tuning, or PSF-stage debugging where the posterior is not needed yet.

knobs.code_doc: Print progress to stdout.
knobs.curated_html: Master verbosity toggle applied to every pipeline stage — progress prints, per-start GD summaries, sampler diagnostics. Does not affect what is written to disk, only console output.

knobs.code_doc: When True (NIFTy + staged joint-PSF only), the PSF Moffat-core parameters remain FREE latents during posterior sampling, so the posterior marginalises over PSF uncertainty instead of freezing the kernel at the final GD value. The background grid stays frozen at its GD value (the 447^2 grid is intractable as VI latents and is pinned by the error-map floor). Requires the staged joint-PSF model (joint_stages set). Set False to reproduce the legacy frozen-kernel sampling exactly.
knobs.curated_html: Keep the PSF Moffat-core parameters as free latents during posterior sampling, so the posterior marginalises over PSF uncertainty instead of freezing the kernel at the final GD value. The background grid stays frozen at its GD value (a ~450² grid is intractable as VI latents and is pinned by the error-map floor). Default false reproduces legacy frozen-kernel sampling exactly.

knobs.code_doc: When marginalize_psf is on, ALSO marginalise the PSF background — but only the high-res pixels inside a central box of side ~ marginalize_psf_background_fwhm_box * fwhm * upsampling (where the PSF carries signal), as a perturbation around the GD-recovered grid. Keeps the sampled-background latent count tiny (= side**2) so geoVI/NUTS stays tractable; the kernel-space prior anchors it to the measured error map. Set False to freeze the whole background (legacy marginalize_psf).
knobs.curated_html: When marginalize_psf is on, also marginalise the PSF background — but only the high-res pixels inside a central box of side ≈ fwhm_box × fwhm × upsampling, where the PSF actually carries signal, sampled as a perturbation around the GD-recovered grid. Keeps the sampled-background latent count tiny (= side²) so geoVI/NUTS stays tractable; the kernel-space prior anchors it to the measured error map.
warnings: Meaningless without sampling.marginalize_psf=true.

knobs.code_doc: Must stay small enough that side = fwhm_box * fwhm * upsampling is below image_size_up; otherwise the box clips to the full grid and the latent count is image_size_up**2 rather than tiny.
knobs.curated_html: Size of the marginalised background box, in units of the PSF FWHM (times the upsampling factor), giving a box of side fwhm_box × fwhm × upsampling centred on the kernel. Only pixels inside the box become free latents. The side is clipped to the full high-res grid, so once fwhm_box × fwhm × upsampling reaches image_size_up, the box covers every background pixel. The example value of 80.0 therefore resolves to the full high-resolution grid if background marginalisation is enabled; in the worked run it is dormant because marginalize_psf is false.

knobs.code_doc: Target posterior sample count after final subsampling. ``None`` keeps whatever the backend produced (no resampling) — with a finite target, backends that produced fewer raw draws than the target are resampled WITH replacement up to it.
knobs.curated_html: Target posterior sample count after final subsampling — the size of the chains written to posterior_samples.npz and used by corner plots and downstream cosmography.
Likelihood-evaluation batch size per device. Larger batches amortise dispatch overhead until memory limits bite.
Number of live points. More live points improve evidence accuracy and multimodal coverage at proportional cost.
Map the unit cube through uniform priors (Nautilus' native parametrisation) rather than the model's transformed priors.
Evaluate the likelihood through the JAX-compiled path (batched, GPU-accelerated) instead of plain NumPy calls.
Distribute batched likelihood evaluations across all available devices.

knobs.code_doc: NIFTy sub-mode, consulted only when the effective sampler is ``"nifty"``.
knobs.curated_html:
NIFTy sub-mode, consulted only when the effective sampler is "nifty":

  • "vi+nuts" — geoVI first, then NUTS-in-ξ refinement warm-started from it. Asymptotically exact, and enables the VI-derived mass matrices.
  • "vi_only" — geoVI only. Fast, but a Gaussian (in ξ) approximation.
  • "nuts_only" — NUTS-in-ξ warm-started from the gradient-descent MAP, skipping VI entirely.

Chain execution strategy. "auto" (the default) picks "parallel" when num_chains ≥ device_count > 1, otherwise "vectorized" — batching all chains into one XLA program, which is roughly a wall-clock factor of num_chains faster than running them one at a time. There is an automatic OOM fallback to "sequential", so "auto" is safe to leave on; set "sequential" explicitly only to force the memory-safe path up front. Note that models above 50000 latent dimensions are routed to a per-chain collector regardless of this setting.

knobs.code_doc: For mass_matrix="block_from_vi": the ξ-leaf names that form the single DENSE block of the mass matrix (everything else stays diagonal). The block is seeded with the geoVI sample COVARIANCE of these leaves, capturing the macro-lens correlations (slope / θ_E / shear / D_dt) that a diagonal mass matrix throws away. None -> the built-in macro-lens default set. Names not present among the live latents are silently skipped.
knobs.curated_html: For mass_matrix="block_from_vi": the ξ-leaf names forming the single dense block (everything else stays diagonal). null uses the built-in macro-lens default set; names not present among the live latents are silently skipped.
Gaussian jitter applied to each chain's initial position — keeps all chains on the typical set (near the warm start) while making them distinguishable, so R-hat is meaningful.

Mass matrix for ξ-space NUTS:

  • "identity" — no adaptation; canonical for standardised ξ-space, but ignores likelihood-induced scale differences.
  • "adaptive_diag" — NumPyro's Welford diagonal estimator during warmup. Robust general default.
  • "diag_from_vi" — per-coordinate variances from the geoVI residual samples.
  • "block_from_vi" — dense macro-lens block seeded from the geoVI sample covariance (slope / θ_E / shear / D_dt correlations that a diagonal matrix throws away), diagonal elsewhere.
Maximum NUTS trajectory tree depth (2^depth leapfrog steps). Chains persistently hitting the cap signal a bad mass matrix — fix that before raising the cap (each +1 doubles the worst-case cost).
Number of chains; null = one per GPU with a minimum of 2, so R-hat is always defined.
Post-warmup samples per chain.
Warmup iterations per chain for NUTS in ξ-space. ξ-space is prior-standardised, but the likelihood still bends it — generous warmup pays off for CF+PSF models.
Target acceptance for step-size adaptation. Raise if divergences appear.
Variational algorithm: "MGVI" (metric Gaussian VI — faster, Gaussian approximation in ξ) or "geoVI" (geometric VI — adapts to posterior curvature, more accurate for non-Gaussian posteriors).
Conjugate-gradient iterations for linear sample draws and KL minimisation. Higher values give more accurate VI samples per iteration at linear cost — the shipped 100 prioritises accuracy.
Scale factor of the random initial position in latent (ξ) space around the warm start.
Total VI outer iterations (KL-minimisation rounds). Watch the reported KL/energy: if it is still falling at the end, add iterations.

knobs.code_doc: batch-resample from converged geoVI; 0 = skip
knobs.curated_html: Batch-resample count from the converged geoVI approximation (posterior samples beyond the few used during convergence). 0 disables and keeps only the convergence samples.
warnings: Ignored when NUTS refinement follows (nifty.mode="vi+nuts") — the NUTS samples overwrite these anyway.

knobs.curated_html: Antithetic sample pairs drawn per VI iteration for the KL estimate. A fixed value is safest; null switches to an adaptive schedule (4→8→16→64).
warnings: The adaptive schedule (null) can OOM on large correlated fields — the late-stage 64-sample rounds are memory-hungry. Prefer a fixed value on big grids.

knobs.curated_html: Fast settings for testing/debugging — reduces conjugate-gradient iteration counts. Not for production posteriors.
PRNG keys per resampling batch; mirror (antithetic) sampling doubles each batch.
Shard the geoVI computation across all GPUs to reduce per-GPU memory — often the difference between fitting and OOM for 128²+ correlated fields.

knobs.code_doc: Stop when the gradient norm of U falls below this.
L-BFGS iteration cap.

``"lbfgs"`` (default): optax L-BFGS with zoom line search on U until ``|grad U| < gtol`` or ``maxiter`` iterations; kept only if U decreased and stayed finite. ``"off"``: the bare exact transfer (0.4.1 behaviour).
knobs.curated_html: After the exact transfer of the GD optimum into the sampler's latent space: "lbfgs" (default) polishes the posterior energy U = −log L + ½|ξ|² with L-BFGS until |∇U| < gtol or maxiter iterations, and keeps the result only if U decreased and stayed finite; "off" uses the bare transfer.

knobs.code_doc: ``True``: stop the run right after the warm start (exact transfer + polish, U and the warm-start diagnostics in ``04_sampling/warmstart/`` written, ``stopped_after_warmstart`` set in ``warmstart_summary.json``) — no geoVI, no NUTS, no posterior. Default ``False`` (sample as configured). Config ``sampling.nifty.warmstart.stop_after`` .
knobs.curated_html: true: end the run right after the NIFTy warm start: exact transfer, polish, the energy U and the warm-start figures and 04_sampling/warmstart/warmstart_summary.json (with "stopped_after_warmstart": true) are written; no geoVI, no NUTS, no posterior. Use it to compare model variants by U on the same data, mask and noise model. Default false.
warnings: sampling.nifty.warmstart rejects unknown keys, so a typo here stops the run instead of silently sampling for hours.

knobs.curated_html: Number of chains. null runs one chain per available device. At least 2 chains are needed for meaningful R-hat diagnostics.
Post-warmup samples per chain.
Warmup (adaptation) iterations per chain — step size and mass-matrix tuning. Lens posteriors with strong D_dt–slope correlations benefit from generous warmup.
Target acceptance probability for the dual-averaging step-size adaptation. Raise towards 0.9–0.95 if divergences appear (smaller steps, slower sampling).

knobs.code_doc: Backend. ``"default"`` auto-selects: NIFTy for correlated-field models, Nautilus for ≤50 parameters, NUTS otherwise.
knobs.curated_html:
Posterior sampler:

  • "nifty" (default): NIFTy inference in the whitened latent space ξ, NUTS and/or geoVI (sampling.nifty.mode). Required for correlated-field sources; also the backend for PSF marginalisation, and the one used by multiband joint sampling;
  • "nuts": NumPyro NUTS on the physical parameters, for shapelet / Sérsic sources of moderate dimension;
  • "nautilus": nested sampling with its own legacy likelihood and MAP-centred empirical priors (restrictions below);
  • "default": NIFTy for correlated fields, Nautilus for ≤ 50 parameters, NUTS otherwise.
warnings: "nautilus" refuses configurations it cannot reproduce: image-plane astrometry (the default), td_common_source true with delays, psf_error_exponent ≠ 1, kinematics, perturbers and a sky background. Its log-evidence uses MAP-centred priors and is not comparable with other engines.

knobs.code_doc: Learning rate of the joint stage.
knobs.curated_html: Adam learning rate for stage 3.

knobs.code_doc: Adam steps of the joint CorrField stage.
knobs.curated_html: Adam steps in stage 3 (cf_joint): a single-start joint optimisation with all latents free (CF source, lens, point sources, PSF), started from the stage-2 state.
Absolute plateau tolerance in nats over one window (default 1.0).

Stop stage 3 on a plateau instead of a fixed budget. The best loss (−log posterior in nats) is sampled every 200 steps; stage 3 stops at step t once best(t − window) − best(t) ≤ max(abs_tol, rel_tol · max(1, |best(t)|)) and t ≥ max(window, min_steps). stages.cf_joint.adam_steps stays the maximum.

With false (default) stage 3 runs its full budget, but the same improvement over the last window is still measured, written to stage3_cf_joint/stage_summary.json (optimizer: stop reason, steps run, best step, convergence) and a WARNING is printed when stage 3 ended on its budget while still improving.
Never stop before this many steps (default 0; the window itself is always a minimum).
Relative plateau tolerance, a fraction of |best loss| (default 0 = off). The larger of abs_tol and rel_tol·|loss| is used.
Steps over which the improvement is measured (default 4000, at least 200).

knobs.code_doc: Run the CorrField joint stage (stage 3): source, lens, lens light and PSF fitted together.
knobs.curated_html: Run the joint CF stage: source + mass (+ PSF in joint-PSF mode, + lens light per stages.cf_joint.lens_light) optimised together, warm-started from the previous stages. This is the stage that produces the MAP model the sampler is centred on. With both CF stages disabled the pipeline is shapelets-only: sampling runs on the stage-1 model.

knobs.code_doc: Optional L-BFGS polish after the joint Adam (0 = off).
knobs.curated_html: Optional L-BFGS polish after the stage-3 Adam run; 0 disables. A few hundred iterations can sharpen the MAP before sampling, at the risk of L-BFGS instabilities on the high-dimensional CF+PSF objective.

knobs.code_doc: 'free' or 'fixed': whether the lens light from the refit stays free in stage 3.
knobs.curated_html: Whether the lens light is "free" (default) in stage 3 or "fixed" at the refit result. Free: the light is fitted together with the source, the mass and the PSF, starting from the refit when light.lens.refit.init_cf_joint is true (default). Fixed: stage 3 fits against the frozen refit light (foreground perturbers are then frozen too, see light.lens.refit.freeze_foreground_perts).
Optional (mean, std) prior of the spectrum's asperity; needs flexibility.
Padding (pixels) of the field grid that is cropped away to avoid periodic-boundary artefacts (default 10).
Optional (mean, std) prior of the spectrum's flexibility; null = off.
(mean, std) prior of the field's fluctuation amplitude (default [1.0, 0.5]).
List of circles [[x, y, r], …] in arcsec (model frame); required for "circles" mode, added to the mask in the other modes.
Dilation of the mask in pixels (default 3).
"model" mode: threshold as a fraction of the peak of the stage-1 plane light (default 0.02; between 0 and 1).

The image-plane mask whose outline, ray-traced to the perturber's plane with the current mass, sets the field's grid extent (the mask does not clip the field):

  • "model" (default): the stage-1 light of that plane, unconvolved, above frac × its peak, dilated by dilate_pix;
  • "circles": the union of circles;
  • "file": a boolean image path on the model grid.

circles given with another mode are added to it.

(mean, std) prior of the amplitude-spectrum slope of the field, as for the source field (default [−3.0, 0.5]). A std far below |mean| fixes it; choose fixed values by cross-validation (alpaca.diagnostics.cf_cv --field pertN).

This key: grid size per side (default 64, at least 4).

Log mean intensity of the field. "auto" (default) = ln(level) + offset_mean_shift, where level is the 90th percentile of the stage-1 light of that plane inside the grid mask (counts per pixel). Or a number.
Shift added to ln(level) by offset_mean: "auto" (default −6: the field starts flat at 0.25 % of the level and grows together with the source in the source-only phase of stage 3).
(mean, std) prior of the zero-mode standard deviation (default [2.0, 0.001]).

knobs.code_doc: Prior centre of the live PSF in stage 3: 'seed' (STARRED seed) or 'stage1'.

"stage1" re-centres the Moffat/background/kernel prior means on the stage-1 recovered PSF (sigmas unchanged) — a trust region around the stage-1 kernel that limits CF↔PSF degeneracy excursions when the flexible source could otherwise trade flux with the PSF wings.

knobs.code_doc: Whether to adapt the source grid extent to the arc mask.
knobs.curated_html: Adapt the source-plane grid extent to the ray-shot arc mask, so field pixels cover the region the arcs actually map to instead of a fixed window. Disable only for controlled comparisons with fixed-grid runs.

knobs.code_doc: Path to a custom mask (FITS or ``.npy``) when mode == "custom".
knobs.curated_html: Path to a custom boolean arc mask (FITS or .npy, matching the image shape). Only read when mode="custom".

knobs.code_doc: Inner radius (arcsec) to mask the lens centre. ``"auto"`` computes from PS positions.
knobs.curated_html: Inner radius masking out the lens centre (lens-light-dominated region). "auto" computes 0.6 × r_min_ps from the innermost point-source radius. 0 disables the central hole — appropriate when the lens light is well modelled and the arcs pass close to the centre.

knobs.code_doc: "auto" = circular annulus from PS positions; "signal" = derived from GD residuals; "custom" = load from ``custom_path``.
knobs.curated_html:
How the arc mask (the image-plane region where the source model is evaluated / the CF grid is anchored) is built:

  • "auto" — circular annulus derived from the point-source positions. Safe default; needs no prior fit.
  • "signal" — derived from gradient-descent residuals: pixels above an SNR threshold, dilated and cleaned. Tightest mask, best CF resolution.
  • "custom" — load a user-provided mask from custom_path.

knobs.code_doc: Outer radius (arcsec) for the source region. ``"auto"`` computes from PS positions.
knobs.curated_html: Outer radius of the source region. "auto" computes 2.0 × r_max_ps from the outermost point-source radius — generous enough for typical quads while excluding field contaminants.

knobs.code_doc: Morphological dilation radius in pixels.
knobs.curated_html: Morphological dilation radius applied to the thresholded signal mask, padding it to include low-SNR arc outskirts adjacent to detected pixels.

knobs.code_doc: Inner radius = ``factor * r_min_ps`` (smaller = let signal decide).
knobs.curated_html: Inner-radius factor for signal mode: a geometric hole of factor × r_min_ps is intersected with the signal mask. The default 0 lets the signal mask alone define the arc, with no central exclusion.

knobs.code_doc: Minimum connected-component area (pixels).
knobs.curated_html: Minimum connected-component area in the signal mask; smaller blobs (noise islands, hot pixels) are removed. Lower it if a genuinely small counter-image is being erased.

knobs.code_doc: SNR threshold for arc detection (mode == "signal" only).
knobs.curated_html: SNR threshold for a residual pixel to enter the signal-derived mask (mode "signal" only). Lower it to catch faint outer arc segments at the cost of noise blobs — which the dilation and minimum-area cleanup then have to remove.

knobs.code_doc: Optional spectral priors. ``None`` disables.
knobs.curated_html: Optional NIFTy spectral prior on the roughness of the power spectrum itself (wiggliness on top of flexibility). null disables; only meaningful together with flexibility.

knobs.code_doc: Legacy source-image truncation is separate from adaptive-grid selection. False keeps PSF-spread source light outside the footprint in the model.
Border pixels cropped to mitigate FFT edge effects.
knobs.curated_html: Border pixels cropped from the field to mitigate FFT periodic-boundary artefacts (the GP is defined on a torus). The field is evaluated on num_pixels + 2·border per side and then cropped back to num_pixels, so the effective source grid stays num_pixels while the sampled latent block is (num_pixels + 2·border)². Increase if bright source flux sits near the grid edge; note the latent count — and therefore NUTS cost — grows with the padded size, not the effective one (at the defaults 80 + 2·20 = 120, that is 14400 latents for a 6400-pixel source).

knobs.code_doc: Whether to exponentiate the field (ensures positivity).
knobs.curated_html: Exponentiate the Gaussian field so the source intensity is strictly positive (log-normal prior). Disabling allows negative source flux — almost never what you want for a physical galaxy.

knobs.code_doc: Optional spectral priors. ``None`` disables.
knobs.curated_html: Optional NIFTy spectral prior letting the power-spectrum slope vary with scale (an integrated-Wiener-process component on the spectrum). null disables. Enable only when a single power law visibly under-fits both large-scale gradients and small-scale clumps.

knobs.code_doc: GP prior hyperparameters. ``loglogavgslope`` controls smoothness (more negative = smoother); ``fluctuations`` controls amplitude.
knobs.curated_html: (mean, std) prior of the fluctuation amplitude of the source field around its mean: how much power goes into structure. Raise it for clumpy, high-contrast sources; lower it if the field starts absorbing noise or lens-light residuals. Fix it together with the slope by cross-validation.

knobs.code_doc: Interpolation method for pixel→image-plane mapping.
knobs.curated_html: Interpolation used to map source-grid pixels onto ray-traced image-plane positions. "fast_bilinear" is the JAX-optimised default; other Herculens interpolators trade speed for smoothness of the gradient.

knobs.code_doc: GP prior hyperparameters. ``loglogavgslope`` controls smoothness (more negative = smoother); ``fluctuations`` controls amplitude.
knobs.curated_html: (mean, std) prior of the average slope of the source field's amplitude spectrum: the smoothness dial (the power-spectrum slope is twice it). More negative = smoother: about −3 for typical hosts, down to −5 or −6 for very smooth sources. The std sets how far the fit may move it.
warnings: Free hyperparameters run to rough fields in a joint MAP fit (the railing report cf_hyperparameters.json flags |z| > 3). Choose the smoothness by cross-validation (python -m alpaca.diagnostics.cf_cv) and fix it with a tiny std, e.g. [-2.5, 0.001].

knobs.code_doc: Log-space mean intensity. ``None`` = estimate from data.
knobs.curated_html: Prior mean intensity of the correlated-field source (the field is exponentiated, so this sets its log-mean). null (default) uses the 70th percentile of the image.
warnings: Together with a tight offset_std (shipped: [0.1, 0.001]) the mean intensity pins the source's log-mean. Once the smoothness hyperparameters are fixed, the default can leave a faint pedestal across the whole source grid (a dark-source residual pattern). Set it to about 0.1 × the noise level so the source is dark where there is no flux.

knobs.code_doc: Number of pixels per side for the source grid.
knobs.curated_html: Source grid size (N×N pixels). Larger grids resolve more source detail and cost more GPU memory (the field has N² latents before cropping). 80 is fine for most arcs; go to 128–256 for extended or highly structured sources.
warnings: Large grids make geoVI memory-hungry — combine with sampling.nifty.vi.use_multi_gpu=true and a fixed n_samples_per_iteration (the adaptive schedule can OOM).

knobs.code_doc: GP prior hyperparameters. ``loglogavgslope`` controls smoothness (more negative = smoother); ``fluctuations`` controls amplitude.
knobs.curated_html: Prior on the field's global offset amplitude — the (mean, std) of the offset's standard deviation in the NIFTy correlated-field model. The tiny default std essentially pins it; loosen only if the overall source normalisation fights the amplitude latents.

knobs.code_doc: Positive scale factor on the adaptive source-plane grid extent derived from the ray-shot arc mask. 1.0 = full footprint (legacy). Use < 1 when the source is compact compared to the mask footprint, so the CF pixels concentrate on the source instead of empty sky.
knobs.curated_html: Shrink factor on the adaptive source-plane grid extent derived from the ray-shot arc mask. 1.0 keeps the full footprint (legacy behaviour). Use < 1 when the source is compact compared to the mask footprint, so the correlated-field pixels concentrate on the source instead of empty sky — effectively raising the source-plane resolution for free.
warnings: Too small a scale crops real source flux; check the source-plane panel of the model summary after changing it.

knobs.code_doc: Must be 'corr_field'.
knobs.curated_html: Source representation of the joint stage — "corr_field" (a pixelated source with a Gaussian-process prior; all the hyperparameters below) is the only supported value.

knobs.code_doc: Learning rate of the source warm-up.
knobs.curated_html: Adam learning rate for stage 2.

knobs.code_doc: Adam steps of the CorrField source warm-up.
knobs.curated_html: Maximum Adam steps in stage 2 (cf_warmstart): a short optimisation over the correlated-field source latents only, with lens, point sources, D_dt and PSF frozen by gradient masking. Early-stopped by patience.

knobs.code_doc: Grow the CorrField source with everything else pinned before the joint fit (phase A of stage 3).
knobs.curated_html: Run the CF warmstart stage: with the stage-1 model (mass, light, point sources) FROZEN, fit only the correlated-field source to the data. Cheap, and gives cf_joint a source that already resembles the arc instead of noise — skipping it makes the joint stage slower and more fragile. Disabled automatically when the pipeline has no CF stages at all.

knobs.code_doc: Early-stopping patience (steps) of the source warm-up.
knobs.curated_html: Early-stopping patience for stage 2: stop when the loss hasn't improved for this many steps.

knobs.code_doc: Adam optimizer settings (shared between phases).
knobs.curated_html: Cosine-decay the learning rate to zero over the run (after warmup) instead of holding it constant — smoother convergence into the basin before L-BFGS takes over.

knobs.code_doc: Adam optimizer settings (shared between phases).
knobs.curated_html: Global gradient-norm clip. Guards against exploding gradients from extreme prior draws in Phase 1.

knobs.code_doc: Adam optimizer settings (shared between phases).
knobs.curated_html: Adam learning rate, shared by both phases (modulated by warmup and cosine decay). Too high loses fragile latents (PSF background, CF spectrum); too low stalls exploration.

knobs.code_doc: Phase-1 Adam steps / L-BFGS iterations per start.
knobs.curated_html: Adam steps per start in Phase 1 (exploration). Enough to reach the basin, not to polish — L-BFGS follows.

knobs.code_doc: Adam optimizer settings (shared between phases).
knobs.curated_html: Fraction of steps spent linearly ramping the learning rate from zero — protects against violent early updates from a bad initialisation.

Adam steps PER LEVEL of the annealing ladder (with anneal.lbfgs_maxiter, default 400, as the L-BFGS counterpart). The per-level budget is deliberately small — the ladder's power is the warm-started sequence, not any single level. adam.steps/lbfgs.maxiter are ignored while annealing is on.

L-BFGS iteration cap PER LEVEL of the annealing ladder — the counterpart of anneal.adam_steps. The per-level budget is deliberately small; the ladder's power is the warm-started sequence, not any single level.

knobs.code_doc: Start noise-inflation level of the `"continuous"` anneal mode (default 16): the likelihood noise is multiplied by this factor at the start and decays exponentially to `level_lo`. Needs level_hi > level_lo ≥ 1. Unused by the `"discrete"` ladder.
Final noise level of the continuous anneal (default 1 = the real noise).

NOISE-CONTINUATION ("annealing") for Phase 1. Each start is optimised at noise_map * level, warm-starting the next level, ending at the TRUE noise (1.0 appended if missing). Inflating sigma by L tempers the imaging likelihood to the power 1/L^2 while priors stay untempered, which smooths away shallow local minima that trap flat multistart (graduated non-convexity / continuation — deterministic, NOT simulated annealing). None/[] = historical single-level behaviour. Deeper schedules (e.g. [16,8,4,2,1]) typically help; Phase-2 refinement still runs afterwards at true noise with the standard refinement budgets.
knobs.curated_html:
Noise-continuation ("annealing") Phase 1. When set, every start is optimised at noise_map × level, each level warm-starting the next, ending at the TRUE noise (a final 1.0 is appended if missing) — so the ranked losses are always the real objective. Inflating σ by L tempers the imaging likelihood to the power 1/L² while the priors stay untempered: the smoothed early levels wash out the shallow local minima plain multistart lands in (graduated non-convexity / continuation — deterministic, NOT simulated annealing).

Benchmarks on real quad-lens data: χ²_red 1.07 vs 1.94 from IDENTICAL starts; 6 annealed starts beat the 30+5 flat recipe at ~21% less compute; the flat baseline's best fit had collapsed the source to a delta function and left the Einstein ring unmodelled. Phase-2 refinement runs unchanged afterwards, at true noise.

knobs.code_doc: ANNEAL MODE . "discrete"   — the ladder above: a fixed noise level per rung. "continuous" — the level decays exponentially from ``anneal_level_hi`` to ``anneal_level_lo`` across ``anneal_segments`` segments. The level is a TRACED argument, so the whole schedule compiles once instead of once per rung. "off"        — no annealing (equivalent to anneal_levels=None). None resolves to "discrete" when levels are set, "off" otherwise, so existing configs keep their behaviour exactly. DEFAULT-ON . Opt out with ``anneal: {mode: "off"}``. NOTE the dataclass default used to be None -> "off"; a config that never mentions annealing therefore CHANGES behaviour on upgrade (faster, equal-or-better chi2, different numbers).
knobs.curated_html:
Noise annealing of the multistart: the likelihood noise is inflated at first and brought down to the real noise, so starts can cross between basins.

  • "discrete": the ladder anneal.levels, a fixed noise factor per rung (default when levels are set);
  • "continuous": the factor decays exponentially from level_hi to level_lo over segments segments; compiles once for the whole schedule;
  • "off": no annealing.

null resolves to "discrete" when levels are set, "off" otherwise.

knobs.code_doc: RAMP the per-rung/segment budget by (index + 1) / n, floored at 50 Adam steps: cheap while the pool is wide and the objective heavily tempered, full budget once the ranking decides. Measured (pool 32, seed 7, identical otherwise): ramp on -> chi2_red 3.83 in 59360 gradients; ramp off -> 8.04 in 106400.  79% MORE compute, and it fails. NOTE: ramping applies cleanly to "discrete" mode only. In "continuous" mode each segment's temperature range is scaled by the same factor so d(log level)/step stays constant -- but that is NOT sufficient: ramped continuous runs still fail (chi2_red 6.1-7.8; 8.5-16.7 without the coupling). A continuous segment must both CONVERGE and TRACK a moving minimum, so it has a minimum viable step count that ramping violates; a discrete rung only has to converge at a fixed temperature. Leave ramp off when mode == "continuous". Stays None: __post_init__ resolves it MODE-AWARE (True for discrete, False for continuous -- a ramped continuous segment violates the 300-step floor and fails).
Number of segments of the continuous anneal schedule (default 5). The level is a traced argument, so the whole schedule compiles once instead of once per rung.

How Phase-1/2 starts are executed. "auto"        — pmap across devices when there is more than one (that parallelism is real), otherwise SEQUENTIAL. "vmap"        — the historical chunked path; keep for reproducing pre- runs. "sequential" / "distributed" — force one. It is worse than neutral: under vmap jaxopt's L-BFGS runs a BATCHED while_loop, so a converged start keeps iterating until its slowest chunk-mate finishes.
knobs.curated_html: How the multistart runs its starts: "auto" (default) spreads them over several devices with pmap when there is more than one device, otherwise runs them one after another; "sequential" / "distributed" force one of the two; "vmap" is the old batched path, kept to reproduce older runs. One start already saturates a GPU, so batching starts on one device does not make them faster.

knobs.code_doc: SUCCESSIVE HALVING over Phase 1: starts alive at each rung/segment. ``[32, 16, 8, 4, 2]`` screens 32 basins for less total compute than the flat recipe spends on 10, because only survivors pay full budget. None = no pruning (every start walks the whole ladder). Must have one entry per rung (discrete) or segment (continuous), and be non-increasing.

L-BFGS implementation. "optax" (default) uses a zoom line search with Wolfe conditions and terminates on the gradient norm; "jaxopt" runs a fixed maxiter regardless of progress and is unmaintained. Keep "jaxopt" to reproduce pre- runs.
knobs.curated_html: L-BFGS implementation: "optax" (default) uses a zoom line search with Wolfe conditions and stops on the gradient norm; "jaxopt" always runs maxiter iterations and is unmaintained, kept to reproduce older runs.

knobs.curated_html: Start a fraction of Phase-1 starts from tight Gaussian perturbations around the prior means instead of full prior samples. Improves convergence markedly when priors are informative (e.g. joint-PSF mode, where PSF priors are seeded); keep some full-prior starts to preserve exploration.

knobs.curated_html: Adam steps per Phase-2 refinement run.

knobs.curated_html: Gaussian σ of the Phase-2 perturbations, in unconstrained (transformed) parameter space.

knobs.curated_html: Reduced-χ² threshold that triggers a retry (when retries are enabled). Also a useful sanity number: a converged fit far above it usually means a data/config problem (wrong pixel scale, missing mask, bad PSF), not bad luck.

A shapelet stage 1 of a quasar lens often ends above 2 even in the right solution, so do not rely on the retry: check the stage-1 and final χ² yourself.

knobs.curated_html: Save the top-N parameter sets from each phase to disk — useful for diagnosing multimodality and for warm-starting later runs.

Phase-1 random starts.
knobs.curated_html: Size of the initial pool of random starts. It is the same number as halving.keep[0]: set one or the other (two different values are refused). null (default) takes halving.keep[0]; without a halving ladder, 32 with annealing and 50 for a flat multistart. A starts without a ladder derives one by halving at every anneal level.

knobs.curated_html: vmap chunk fallback ladder for multi-start GD — how many starts are batched through one vmapped evaluation, largest tried first with OOM fallback down the ladder. Hardware-dependent: [10, 5, 1] is fastest on ≥ 40 GB cards; the conservative default is required on 24 GB cards with ~200² frames.
warnings: A failed large-chunk attempt fragments the GPU memory pool (anomaly 003) — on smaller cards, don't lead with an optimistic chunk size.

knobs.code_doc: Maximum shapelet order of the stage-1 source.
knobs.curated_html: Maximum Shapelet order. The number of basis functions grows as (n_max+1)(n_max+2)/2 — n_max=16 gives 153 components. Higher orders resolve finer source structure but add latents and can start fitting noise or absorbing PSF residuals. Unused unless source_type="shapelets" or the staged CF flow (whose stage 1 is a Shapelets fit).

knobs.code_doc: Source model of the GD stage: shapelets | sersic | double-sersic | corr_field. 'shapelets' is required for the staged CorrField pipeline.
knobs.curated_html: Source representation used during the stage-1 multi-start gradient descent. "shapelets" (Sersic + shapelet basis, size n_max) is the production default — smooth, analytic and fast to optimise from random starts. "sersic" drops the shapelets. "corr_field" runs GD directly on a pixelated correlated-field source (no staged flow; expensive and non-convex — the staged shapelets → CF path exists precisely because this is hard).
